representative_reviews.text: I bought 2 Moab2 shoes one for myself at REI and one for my son via Amazon . I am very unhappy and disappointed with both the shoes. Both of us get blisters on our both of out foot soles any time we go for a walk hike which lasts more than half hour. This has never happened to us before with any shoe. We differ in height, weight, shoe size, style of walking, but we both end up having blisters on our feet. Both of us are fit and can usually hike moderate to challenging trails upto 10 miles with no problems of course in other footwear . In addition, we notice that the front part of the shoe has very little cushioning and we can 'feel' the road its very uncomfortable. I had very high expectations this is my first Merrell purchase and I cannot be more disappointed. I would discourage people from buying this product blisters, inadequate cushioning in front, in general, uncomfortable . I would give a 0 star rating if I could.

I ruck. 30lb pack, walk a few miles. Been doing it with another pair of Merrels for 2 years. From the first I thought it was because I was doing different exercises. Took a while then I realized the inside of the left heel was probably 1 4 taller than the outside. Hence I was walking on the inside 50 of my heel. The other half wasn't touching. After 3 weeks, the pain in my heel was constant. Stopped using them. I took another 2 weeks for my feet to go back to normal. I've had Merrels for years. There is definitely something wrong with this batch. If you feel pain, stop using them immediately.

When I put these on I could immediately tell that something was not right. The arch support was not on the arch of my foot, but instead it rested back towards my heel and not just a little bit. I ve never had a problem with the arch on any other shoe. Sticking her finger inside the shoe to feel where the arch hit my foot, my wife could tell that it was way off. I know that different people have different feet, but I don't think any human has a foot that this shoe could satisfy. Searching through the reviews again for the word heel, I could see that others had the same problem. I had to return the shoes. If not for this defect, these are good looking shoes that I probably would have enjoyed.

VIDEOID c885b9f6f936b9b21a087fc15be39b16 I have worn MOABs for many years. Love them. I have issues with rolling my left ankle and sweaty feet. The original MOAB solved everything. I was concerned to hear the "MOAB II" had replaced the product I loved, so I called Merrell's Customer Service about it. They told me that the MOAB II was the same product, but with improved materials. So, I ordered a new pair. It turns out that Merrell's assertion was patently false. There are IMPORTANT differences that cause my ankle to be unsteady. Less ankle area padding, one less shoestring eyelet for final cinching, and lack of the stiffener that stabilizes the upper foot at the ankle. I posted a video. See for yourself.
Inserts are garbage, but I guess I'll buy some inserts so i can use them. One 10 hour shift at a factory and my feet feet hurt like heck.

I wore these shoes hiking 5 miles and my feet hurt for 3 days after. I am an avid hiker and this literally has never happened before. I broke them in first before going hiking and it did not help. I am outside the return period so these will be getting donated although I almost feel guilty allowing someone else to wear them. DO NOT BUY THESE.

I switched to these and instantly got Plantar Fasciitis and bad bad foot pain just like some of the other reviewers. They are not made with even 50 percent of the quality they had before. I've bought the same Ventillators design for about 15 years now. This is the first pair I've bought since they changed them and they suck. My wife bought a pair and has had discomfort and heel slippage. I used to work at R E I in the shoe dept. and I have to say these have gone downhill and bad. Save yourself the injury and the money and look at other brands.

I've been wearing Merrell shoes for years. I had one other pair that didn't last very long, but generally I feel like they are a reasonable deal for their price. This pair is ridiculously bad. They were painful on the heels, but I figured new insoles would probably resolve that problem and I missed my return window by trying different insoles. I've had three different insoles in them besides the cheap ones that came with the shoes. A pair of Superfeet insoles makes them almost bearable. However, they are still not comfortable and definitely won't be useful as a hiking shoe. I am literally in pain after walking less than a couple of miles with the other three insoles. I don't know if my pair has a manufacturing defect or what, but these shoes are killing my heels. None of my other shoes Merrell or otherwise have ever caused me pain in my heels. It is like somebody placed an uncomfortable rock within the heels of the shoes.

Update after wearing for two days I can t walk anymore. Do not buy them. I have to go see a doctor because I I think I have bone spurs in both heels. I ve bought merrels for years. These are the worst buy ever. My heels have hurt for three days straight. I would suggest buying a special gel insole.
Shoe is extremely uncomfortable. Could not wait to get home and get them off. Would love to return them for a refund.

The shoes hurt my feet,unfortunately. Burning all day. Middle of shoe bed hurt as well. I'm a bigger person, so maybe these shoes would work for someone smaller. I should tried them on ,before purchasing.

It felt like there was a valley running down the middle of the shoe. I could feel support on either side of my foot, but not in the middle. That actually made it feel like there were bumps on the sides. Perhaps an after-market insole would correct that. Also, the shoe seemed long enough but it seemed like my foot would slide forward causing my big to to hit the front. I tightened the laces more and that helped some.

I work in security. I bought these shoes because I like the brand Merrell and because I walk a lot thought maybe I would use them for patrol. But lately there shoes have began to degrade in quality. I have bought two different pairs. I wore them with the original inserts which came with the shoes and Ended up getting blisters in the back of my feet and toes. Then I put better insert In now the toes I get blisters. These shoes are not vented. My feet sweat so bad. I even wear IQ socks to prevent sweat and they also wic it off as well. I wish I could get my money back for this product but there is no way in heck that is going to happen. Only wore them for two weeks and they couldn t even handle that on patrol let alone if you re going out in the wilderness for long periods of time.

I bought the Merrell Moab 2 Vent Hiking boots. They felt awesome when I first got it. Kind of heavy and soles were hard but that was to be expected from hiking shoes. I believe another reviewer wrote in pretty good details why he she believed it was causing pain. I thought it may have been a one off but I think it was pretty accurate because after a few weeks of use. I wear to work though it's a office job, it's casual . After a few weeks I noticed my feet were hurting. I believe so were my knees and ankles but I the pain wasn't noticeable then. Over time they all started to hurt more and more. I initially thought I was just out of shape since I was walking more at night with my regular running shoes. Over time, the pain continued and so I stopped wearing them. Well, it's been about 3 weeks since I last wore these boots, my walking walking is the same, but the pain has lessened by a lot. Only my ankle still remains a bit stiff. Anyway, I really love the fit, style and feel of the shoes, unfortunately something about it is causing damage to me such that I may just donate them. 3 stars because I want to love them but I just can't.

These Moab 2 Hikers hurt walking just a short distance. The base of the shoe is hard. Haven't gone long distance yet based on this. For a 90 pair of shoes, I'd expect comfort. Nope. Need to go buy insoles for more . Arch support is moderate. the toe box is odd. If I move my toe upward, my toenail can hook on the stiffer portion of the toe box. Based on other reviews here I was concerned that the fit of the Moab 2 Ventilator shoes would be worse than the prior version. I was very pleasantly surprised that this was not the case. I find the Moab 2's to be better out of the box than the Moab version. My last pair of Moabs left me with blisters until after a very long break in period. They were tight at the top and the blisters were on the outside of my right heel. The new Moab 2's have been extremely comfortable immediately. I have put on about 15 miles so far of quite hilly street walking and find these shoes very comfortable and I have had no issues with either blisters or tightness. I actually like the change in the lacing pattern as it fits the top of my foot better than the predecessor version. I have had no issues with heel looseness at all. I haven't noticed any increase in arch support as some have noted, but am happy with the stability the shoes provide. For background, I have been wearing Moabs for many years starting with the regular ones and shifting to the ventilated models over the past three or four years. Update after four months Shoes remain extremely comfortable. I walk 5-7 miles a day on rough paved roads. Last pair of Moab vents went about 9 months before the soles were too worn down to use. These Moab 2's seem to be wearing a bit more so far. I doubt I will get six months before needing to replace them. This is unfortunate as the uppers and insoles are still in great shape.

Fits well thought the arch support is prominent. I have liked Merrell short hikers in the past, as they have been supportive and worked well for hiking but I've have had bad luck with them falling apart prematurely torn upper in one pair, fractured sole in another . Well, soon I ll be going on a descent long term hike averaging 20 - 30 miles a day for about a week. I ll take these shoes on the trip and write back later about my experience.

I've never spent much money on shoes since I started buying my own. As a result I developed plantar fasciitis. I've really struggled with finding the right shoe with the right kind of support. Some shoes that are great for arches make my shins hurt. I've gotten into the habit of swapping out shoes on a nearly daily basis - a tactic that seems to work. SO I bit the bullet and started buying better shoes with more support. BTW - best shoes for PF are Durango Rebel cowboy boots. The full heel keeps you from twisting your ankle and the rise helps stretch those muscles in the right way. Back to the Merrell Moab it's a great shoe. I wanted a hiking shoe to wear with cargos and something that would be a bit more comfortable that cowboy boots to wear when walking or hiking of course . I could immediately feel the difference. This is a well made shoe with lots of support. I would give the shoe a 5, but they just don't quite make it. The only problem I have with the Moab is that they wear a bit tight in the middle and seem a bit large in the toe box. I have more of a narrow to normal foot and I definitely cannot wear a wide. This shoe is on the narrow side and if I tie them tight my foot will start going numb. My solution is to tie them a bit loose.
I bought the hiking boots for a trip to Mt. Lacont, they were so comfortable I bought these shoes and I wear them everyday!! Highly recommend!

Very comfortable and I've worn them every day now for two months, 12 hours each day, and they seem very durable, still look like the day I got them! minus all the dust on them

Merrell makes a quality product and this shoe in particular is comfortable and provides good support for light hiking. The shoes I take on all trips and they have been good and held up from Nepal and India to Switzerland and Denmark.

I've owned Merrill ahoes before and as anticipated they are one of the most comfortable shows have worn. I walk an average of 8 to 10 miles every day at work and my feet don't hurt. I would recommend them to anyone

I'm 44 and have been through a pair or two of shoes in my time. These shoes come as close to the ideal shoe for me as I'm sure is possible. The mesh built throughout the body of the shoe makes for great ventilation, and soles are grippy in pretty much every condition. They even handle walking on wet driftwood logs with ease. The footbeds are soft enough to provide comfort, but aren't pronounced enough to be a hindrance to those with lower arches like mine. Those with higher arches will likely need to add their own inserts that accommodate the shape of their feet. While water can easily get into these shoes, it's not really that bad an issue, because it can evaporate out quickly with the mesh. The one drawback I have for these shoes is pretty much a universal problem for fabric shoes, and that is sand. When you're walking in sand, it gets into pretty much every one of those vents and can be problematic to remove. During the hike through sand, you'll feel the shoe become significantly heavier due to the sand. The only thing I've found that works is taking them off after an hour or so of hiking, and beating them against driftwood to dislodge the sand. I'm sure that walking in the dunes will produce the same problem. All in all, though, I love these shoes and I've put a lot of miles on my prior pair. This purchase is to replace my old pair. If you're looking for reliability through pretty much anything the trail can throw at you they even handle walking on snow and ice relatively well with ease. I highly recommend these for everyone, with exception to trail runners. These shoes are light to me, but lead weights to those who want the absolute bare minimum for weight.
This will be a very good hiking shoe. The arch is stiff and it will take a little time to get the shoe to feel right. After that, they are a heat shoe. Still kinda stiff.

I have worn Merrell shoes for almost fifteen years, and have worn Merrell Moab for at least the last seven or eight years. I have hiked many miles on Merrell Moab and on other shoes. They have been a go to general, all-around hiker in my house for a long time. They just did everything pretty well. That has changed. Even though I contacted Merrell about the changes, which they said were basically cosmetic and material, that is not true. It is an outright lie. The last and sizing are very different. The shoe is at least a half size larger. Moving down a half size will not likely give you the fit you need due to an oddly different way that the shoe rolls from heel to toe. The heel - toe movement is far different. You will feel like you are wearing high heels. It will not properly grip at the heel and then roll toward the toe. It has an odd movement. The arch is now in the wrong location. It does not matter what size you try. The arch is different. You will need to replace the footbed. The heel ankle support is very different and less supportive. It will feel as if there is less cushioning in the front of the foot. Basically, I cannot afford to wear a shoe that will not give me the support and response I need. I walk and hike regularly. It breaks my heart that I will no longer be able to wear Merrell Moab, but this Moab 2 is not worthy of being called a general, all purpose hiker. It has changed.

For example five years ago one could expect this model to last perhaps 50 longer than today. The specific flaw is in seam glue where front rubber material separates from canvas leather type material. representative_reviews.text: Like other reviewers here, I have been a long time devotee of Keen. I've had probably a half dozen pairs or so over the years. I've loved the heck out of them... until now. I just ordered a pair of the Targhee IIs like the last 3 pairs I've had and they are totally different in fit, feel, and construction. And of course, they're not made in Oregon anymore, but now they're made in Thailand. I have wide feet and have always had a great fit with these, now they're almost a size too small, and far, far too narrow. Horribly uncomfortable whereas before I could put them on out of the box and be good to go. I'm so, so sorry to see Keen lose the quality and fit they used to have when they were made here. I guess it's time to move on, and begin my search for a new brand. These are going back.
Left big toe sore. Can t figure out why. Right shoe is good fit even with narrow feet. Shoe looks faded after a week s wear.
Had the boots 2 months and the rubber heel has already peeled off. Contacting Keen to see about a replacement. Disappointed!
Reasonably comfortable and no break-in blisters. Negative is the shoe tongue design. Sides if shoe do not fully cover tongue when laced up. You have to adjust ever time.

Returning these-fit is terrible for me. The toe box is wider but yet not enough room for my big toe and would cause blisters. The opening heel is too large and would slide off. Also there is weird support lift on the outer base of the foot which negates the arch support. Just a weird fit overall. Not impressed.

I'm disappointed in having to give these shoes a low rating but unfortunately the bad outweighs the good. From the bit I've used them, they seem very sturdy and like they'd stand up to a good bit of hiking walking. Having bought other KEEN brand shoes, I wouldn't doubt this to be the case. The problem comes with how the shoe fits. The laces do not tighten well up near the top of the shoe. It's both too small and too big at the same time. Down at the toes it's too small. Any amount of walking, especially on uneven ground crushes my toes. At the same time it's so lose in the back of the shoe my heel is coming out with every step. With how poorly the laces tighten up the shoe, there isn't a good way to get around this. A half size up and my whole foot would slip out of the shoe. A half size down and I'd be losing toes. After a mere 5 hour work shift, and 6 miles of walking, I have significant pain in my feet and blisters on my toes. Will not be wearing them again.

As always Keen is a comfortable shoe for my feet, but I was very disappointed that this shoe was labeled black. The color is more like wet dirt or a greyish brown. I needed black shoes, not gray or brown.

bought these for my son, he is replacing a greenhouse roof with a metal roof, it is really steep, wanted to make sure he was safe, got all the equipment to keep him on the roof, he needed a new pair of shoes so I looked up the best roofing shoes, out of all the designs, he liked these the best because he would be wearing them on off the roof, well he put them on while standing on a piece of plywood, to make sure he didn't carry anything onto the metal roof, after he got tied off got onto the metal roof, he started slipping sliding all over, I had to pitch his old shoes to him, Sketchers tennis shoes, and he could stand up without losing his footing, these shoes ARE NOT SAFE!

Not sure i would buy a keen product again. Have had the shoes 5 months now and the left shoe squeaks when you walk. Have always gotten Merrills but thought I would spend a little more and give these a try, while the waterproof factor has been good Im pretty disappointed.

These KEEN Targhee II hikers stink like no other shoe I have purchased from KEEN or any other brand. Literally, they are emitting an odor as they sit on the floor next to me, dry, in an air-conditioned environment and having not been worn for nearly two weeks. I can't wear these shoes indoors and around other folks any more because they really smell. This is not the typical new shoe odor which I usually enjoy and which also normally dissipates after several uses. This smell is materials related and is a cross between armpit and synthetic shoe adhesive. Due to the design of the shoe with the KEEN Dry water proofing membrane material , the shoe doesn't breath at all. As a result, my feet get really hot and sweat profusely. Over 1.5 year's time and with very limited, occasional use literally once a month if that , these Targhee IIs started emitting an odor about 6 months in and like I have never experienced before. This shoe has never been soaked through on a muddy trail and looks brand new. This shoe has had odor prevention spray applied multiple times on the interior. I keep these stinkers in an dry environment. Normally, those measures keep the smell-factor down or mitigate it completely with my footwear. Not with the Targhee IIs. Have you ever realized partway though the day that deodorant was not applied that morning due to the sudden essense-of-pit hitting the olfactory? That's the surprise awaiting me if I don these slippers of smell and falsely hope that today is the day that I've rid these shoes of their stench. I suspect that an adhesive used in the shoe construction does not interact well with hot feet and, in turn, I feel like it is important to state that I've worn KEEN shoes with better air circulation for well over a decade and, while they get smelly over time, that's a normal thing and can be addressed. Due to my experience with these malodorous moccasins, I'm skittish about buying any KEEN product with their KEEN Dry membrane due to the lack of breath-ability and materials used. If you are thinking about buying the Targhee II for any type of indoor work or even going out on a date wearing them, then don't. Unless your partner is into weird industrial organic-industrial odors. If so, then you are in luck!

I have been wearing Keens for years. Started with a pair of Newport sandals and expanded from there. I have a pair of their work boots as well. I bought this pair of Targhees in March of 2017 as a replacement for a similar pair that I had for many years and just plain wore out. I mostly use these shoes for walking, not strenuous, just for leisure. Perfect fit, great shoe.... until the black tread part of the sole began to detach from the shoe. The upper part of the shoe looks great and has many years of life left. But the black sole is definitely coming off. I contacted Keen but they coldly informed me that they only warranty for one year. I just ordered some barge cement Keen's suggestion from Amazon and hope I can repair them myself. Maybe I shouldn't expect shoes to last more than a year but I do. Especially at these prices. Buyer beware -apparently Keens aren't what they used to be.

I recently tested this shoe on a 39 day hiking trip that averaged about 8 miles per day. The terrain grip was excellent in a variety of conditions and surfaces though I did have a few slips on wet surfaces. The shoe runs a little hot and causes some serious foot sweat and stench but that is likely a result of the very protective leather exterior. I don't always retie my shoes and wedge my foot into the shoe and this has caused the rear seam to tear very quickly. The laces don't cinch down the different areas of the shoe very well and don't hold the tightness well either. It leaves you with an unsecured feeling, especially in the toes. On the days that were over 10 miles, my feet were left hurting and the tip of my second toe on both feet was in a lot of pain. I would return these shoes if I could to take a shot at a different pair. The toe of the shoe did seem large and durable though.
The shoe runs small by at least 1 2. Hard sole, not comfortable to walk with. Bad value for even half the price I paid
These shoes were scratched up , looked terrible . Husband said he'll use them cause there still new shoes but wow

Not as comfortable as I d hoped. The heal sticks out the back and is awkward. 5 month update. Starting to come apart and make a funny noise when I walk. Hardly worn them and now they re going to hell. Zero stars. Wondering is there s a warranty

I've worn this brand and this style for years they have made some improvents to the insole and arch support which seems comfort...Thank you Keen.
I have always loved Keen hikers... Nice high arch, toe protection, walked two hours in 4" snow stayed warm and dry. Plenty of room for my wide foot

The minute you put the shoes on your entire body is in alignment, your feet, knees, hips, and spine. I have better posture when wearing my Keens. Of all the brands I own Keens by far are the most comfortable.

This is my third pair of these boots bc i wore out the other pairs from hiking and walking dogs. Great pair, good toe room for people with bunions and stiff arch. I use a different foot liner but these are great boots if you need arch support. Glad Keen continues to make them for people with problem feet

The toe box is roomy which is something I require for shoes which will get a lot of mileage. There is great tread for walking on trails. So far I m happy with the water resistance. Cons Despite having the opportunity for tightening the heal of the shoe, I m still getting some movement which makes me nervous for longer walks of 10 or more miles. There is less cushioning in this Keen than in my other two pairs, so I do feel discomfort in the balls of my feet after long walks.
I have been wearing Keen shoes for about 12 yrs. Not only are they comfortable they have a lot of support. I wear them every day and also have a pair for hiking. Great show, only ones I buy.
It is comfortable and useful, not so hot and not cold definitely My favorite shoe in light winter as we have Thanks

Purchased for light hiking and wearing for work in really bad weather I do home care nursing . I hesitate to buy shoes online but these are so comfortable and waterproof. My foot is on the wide side and I have a high arch so it's hard to find shoes that fit, are comfortable and have good support. I anticipate several years of comfortable use from these.

Excellent for hiking and just typical wear around town walking shoes - very durable sole and uppers. I use "super-feet" insoles bad arches in my feet so I can't comment on the insoles of the shoe itself. But, if they're as good as the rest of the shoe - I'm sure they're fine for people who don't need additional arch supports. Overall comment Great Product!
Great hiking shoe. Comfortable enough to walk around airport for 8 hours then hiking in Utah. Highly recommend

I have feet that are difficult to buy shoes for. I had surgery on my big toe to remove part of the bone because it was growing together, so I have to have shoes that provide a thick enough sole. My favorite shoe boot all day comfort right out of the box. I have a really wide foot and these boots can accommodate a 4E.

I love Keen shoes, boots and sandals. If you have a wide forefoot I do This footwear is the best. I do have one complaint, and that is the sizing. It is not consistent from style to style. So in the Keen Presido I wear 8B. but in Keen sandals 9B. In the European sizes sometimes 39, other times 39.5. I have two pairs of hiking boots in mens size 7 for a bit more width Both are marked 39.5. One is a bit longer than the other. If you need a wide shoe it is well worth the effort to find the size you need in the style you are looking at. These are well made, the insole is removable for those who need to customize the support, the waterproofing Keendry membrane is excellent. I have worn these type Keen waterproofed shoes and boots year round and they do not feel hot to me, any more than any boot or shoe with this type of construction. The tongue is bellowed to help keep water and other junk out. The sole is great for rough irregular or just hard surfaces, providing grip and protective cushion.. Took a few tries to get the lacing tied comfortably. They need minimum break in, if any, and I expect them to hold up well with normal care. . I like this shoe, and once I dialed in the size I got a second pair in another color. My experience with this brand says it will be a long happy relationship.

A shame, because every other part of the shoe fits me perfectly - to where if I exchanged for a bigger size, everything else would be too loose. As an outdoorsy type with PF, I'm always looking for a durable shoe that doesn't kill my feet while I'm working. It could use a bit more cushion built in not the insert, I use ones my podiatrist recommends , but it's far better for all day field work than any North Face, Columbia or Merrill shoe I've tried. For the record, I waited until I've worn them through three field trip cycles and machine washed once before reviewing. They seem like they should last a year or more. Nice and roomy up front for toe stretching.

I just bought my 3rd pair. I wear them most days. Each of the past 2 pairs has lasted around 3 years before I wore through the soles. I bought them again because they have held up so well. Hopefully this pair does equally as good.
Just got these today but impressed with the quality and support. I shouldn t be as this is my 2nd pair of Keen s in 7 years and the first pair were super durable.
A great outdoor shoe. It's not a high top, so there's no additional ankle support, but they are great, solid shoes.

This is after a year of use. The Thailand made shoes don't live up to the Keen standard that I used to know. I think I'll try to find Patagonia like shoes that are like these hopefully they still have quality made in America shoes... Hell it doesn't even matter to me where they are made as long as the quality is there, I don't get how shoe companies don't realize this. Update. After this review I took the purchase order from Amazon and the photos to the customer service people at Keen. They gave me money to buy another pair of shoes on their site! So I'm happy with the support but really not the product. I mean I can already see issues with the new pair I bought quality wise and they were 130 dollars... I upped the stars to 3 from 2 in this case for the support.

My husband uses these for work. They are the only shoe that lasts him and he doesn t tear up. He normally buys them for around 150. We got these for 70 and consider it a steal. We will buy again next year when he s ready for new shoes. We won t have to worry about new work shoes till then because these hold up so well!

This is my 4th pair of these shoes, I wear them every day and they provide great stability, breathable and dry. I am very hard on my shoes and they are extremely durable! I love that they can be totally wet on the outside and completely dry on the inside. Highly recommended.

I've had 2 pairs of the Targhee mid-height hikers and since breaking my ankle and having metal plate and screws put in over a year ago, I can't tolerate any boot that comes up over or above the ankle bone for very long. These were the perfect solution - same solid stability, traction and warmth but just below the ankle bone like a sneaker.
As a member of USPS I need shoes that will hold up in the southern wet weather while being comfortable and safe. These shoes fit the bill! Will continue to buy these exact shoes.

KEEN wearer for years. Needed another pair for all weather conditions. These are comfortably supportive of my old flat feet and offer my toes the wiggle room they need while keeping them dry to boot. Another winner from KEEN. Picture shows the models Flint steel toe ,Targee 2 and Circadia from top to bottom.

I have been wearing these for a couple of months, and they are holding up well so far. Worn them on dewy grass without getting my feet wet. My only issue is that the soles can be a little slippery on loose ground. If this is a concern, the Targhee 3 might be a better option.

representative_reviews.text: Cheap, much worse quality in person than is evident in the photos. Looks roughly the same coming out of the box, but upon closer scrutiny, you can immediately make out areas where it's prone to come apart within months of average daily use. Having bought a lot of shoes over the years, the signs were all recognizable. This is not the quality we expected from Keen's and I purchased based on old reviews, hoping the naysayers just got a rare instance of bad QA. But looking at the manufacturing, it seems like the obsolescence is either built in or they're just cutting corners behind the scenes to stabilize their retail pricing in the face of inflation. Maybe supply chain issues? But sadly, this seems to be the norm. I read wayyyy too many reviews trying to find the perfect shoe for someone who works outdoors, and Salomon Saucony appear to have formerly been the best alongside Keens, but now followed suit in terms of quality decline. Three brands that used to mean quality people swore by, and brands that still aren't cheap at all. Shoes you buy for a few hundred bucks so you won't, theoretically, have to go out and by another pair in a few months. It seems criminal that they aren't lasting as long as the Payless shoestore cheapies. This appears to have gotten especially pervasive in the past 2 years - maybe due to COVID, somehow? Did people stop buying shoes except house slippers? What was going on? Who knows. But that's where the good reviews on major upper-midscale shoe brands start to get disillusioned and bitter. With the exception of Timbos. My kid bought some Timberlands last year, and they were as high quality as the pair hubs bought 2 years ago, which are still going 100 strong today, with no sign of wearing down, despite rough daily use in the field. Side note - Doc Martins plummeted in quality similarly about 10-15 years ago. They stopped making them in the UK, and even a newish UK pair I got back then wasn't as on point as a pair my friend had from 10 years prior. So Keens held out a little longer, at least. Side note this was the 2nd pair of Keens my husband tried in the past 4 years. So I don't think it could be all COVID, because we noticed a quality decline even back then. The last pair he got in 2018 was a work boot advertised as waterproof and was not even slightly so, not even brand new. Broke down after about 6 months, as well. We're done with this brand.

After 4 months of light use the plastic sides started to peel back. The last pair took 2 years before falling apart. This is more disappointed and would not buy these again not worth the money for the quality.
Really it does have good material but some parts of tbe seams are getting undone I have wear them 3 time and already failing

These used to be very fine quality shoes. Nowadays, these are suffering from poor quality and thin materials. The leather is so thin and the overall quality has really suffered. Don't recommend anymore.

Cheap quality, lasted less than 30 days, Maybe wore 15 times, broken top lace eyelet atrap... garbage. Too bad, had a pair of their old closed toe sandals that lasted 15 years... these lasted 15 walks around the neighborhood.

Now manufacturing is done in India. Was manufactured in Thailand for years. They are different shoes. The fit is loose and the soles are missing something as they are less padded. I own 11 pairs of these according to Amazon and they last two have been returned as they don't meet the standard or of the box. The machine that makes the shoes is different and it shows in the product. I will look for keens made in Thailand not India. I should have known something was up when they price dropped by almost half and the box that came was smaller than any keen shoe box I have received. Got to cram more boxes into a shipping container right?
I bought these just over a month ago and they are already falling apart. Not impressed at all. Keen has gone way down hill with quality!

I am a fan of Keen shoes, but this pair disappointed me. The glue started coming apart after only 34 days, and that point, I was past the window of returning. I don t feel that a shoe with this price should start falling apart after minimal wear in a 34 day period.

Im very disappointed with this shoes Im a Keen fan since long time ago I bought several pairs of shoes in the past, but the last two pairs looks like their quality is low I only wear this shoes two days and the front plastic toe protector got unstick very easy on the seam looks like they use a cheap glue or something hopefully I can get my refund back otherwise what a waste of money!!

Over the years I've purchased Keen hiking shoes many times. However, my two most recent purchases have shown a sharp decline in the quality which I believe corresponds to their manufacturing being move to China. In my case, the sole of the shoe has been coming apart. This shouldn't be happening to a shoe costing as much as these do and for the purpose hiking that they are supposedly made for. I'll probably but this brand again.

Keen quality has drastically subsided. While they fit as expected and appeared to be the quality you would expect from Keen, they came unglued after six weeks. And because I am outside the return window, now stuck with a poor quality of expensive shoes. I used these for casual outdoor project work, nothing strenuous or on severe terrain. No chemical exposures or anything that would warrant rapid failure. Disappointed in Keen. My only option is to provide warning to others looking to purchase who have also trusted Keen in the past.

My husband has been wearing these Keene's for years. Always had a great experience with them and they last forever. Until now. Like everything else in the world, cheap is the way to go. I noticed out of the box these felt lighter and flimsier than his previous pair and sure enough, after one wear on a light walk, the lace holders began to tear. I returned. Not sure I will try these again. We turned to these after years of another top brand that did the same thing.....cheaped out....now after 12 years of Keene...it might be time to move on again.

this is my 9th pair of Keens... ever since they sold out to china their quality has gone down the toilet. If you want your shoes to fall apart in literally 2 weeks buy keens. VERY DISAPPOINTED ANOTHER AMERICAN COMPANY SOLD OUT!

This brand used to be good. Purchased in November, didnt wear at all in December or January due to deep snow. Its now April and I've only worn them for walks in the neighborhood and shopping trips, and theyre already falling apart. The cheap foam that connect the sole to the leather shoe shreds so easily and is separating in several places. Will not buy KEENs again.

Used to have Keen Shoes same type and were comfortable for daily use. This one does not seem to be made that well, materials are hard as rock. Its made overseas, quality is just not there. I returned it.
Simply put. This is the best shoe on the market for what they are intended. I am a huge fan of Keen.

Originally my wife purchased a pair from an REI store. They lasted 6 years before they finally needed replacing, but not because they were broken. She still wears them to work in the yard. The only reason she bought a 2nd pair was because the other didn't look nice anymore. We did find that this pair doesn't seem to have quite as high of an arch as the original pair, but overall she is very satisfied and recommends them to all of her friends. Prior to buying Keens she would get lots of ankle and calf pain when walking. Now she can walk all day on any type of flooring or ground and no pain. I'd say that's a win!
Great shoe. After the last pair wore out I tried another brand, Columbia, they started to fall apart in 6 months. Went back to the Keen's and am happy.
Great feel and fit, look good also.The advice to go one half size larger worked out good. Nice shoes. That's why I ordered a second pair, different color of course!
Just got these today but impressed with the quality and support. I shouldn t be as this is my 2nd pair of Keen s in 7 years and the first pair were super durable.

I know these are a little pricey but they are worth it! I have never liked hiking shoes or boots as they always felt so heavy and constricting. However, these are just a little heavier than a good supportive pair of sneakers. But most importantly, the fit is great. Especially in the toes because it's not a super tight feel, like many other shoes I tried on. I used these on trails but also on concrete because they are waterproof. They were fantastic.
My husband loves the color He has been buying Keen's for sometime and had me put the same shoes on his wish list for the future.

Having just purchased a pair of Targhee II Keens and a pair of Targhee III Keens over the last couple months, I've been able to discern what I believe is the better model, at least for me. The Targhee II has a better sole pattern, Laces and seems to be a little heavier duty. The fit on both was fine, but walking in the woods and on snow, I definitely prefer the Targhee II. I will purchase a couple more pairs so if they are discontinued, I'll be set for quite a while.

First pair was a pretty decent pair of shoes given the garbage market we re in today. I wouldn t say that they were the best pair I ve ever owned but I m also pretty hard on my shoes. I m a big guy and when I find a pair I wear them all day every day until they wear out. This pair fits true and appears well made. The last pair started separating at the toe cap and the leather got too soft to hold its shape any more. I think these are gonna do the same, but I got a good six months to a year out of the last pair. We ll see if these hold up.
NOT ONLY DID I GET A GREAT PRICE THE BOOTS ARE FANTASTIC.THE GRIP IS GREAT,FEEL GREAT ON THE FEET AND LOOKING FORWARD TO A LOT OF WALKING

Awesome shoe for just about everything. I average about 5 mile a day in trail walking and this shoe is perfect. I notice that keen change the innersole which I think was not a good fit. Other than that, it is perfect.

I purchased these shoes locally the first time. Now for repeat purchases I just ordered them from Amazon. They are well-built and last a long time excellent daily shoe. Work well for working and hiking. I also like the stylish look.

This hiking shoe is everything one would expect from KEEN. It's well-constructed, good looking, and sturdy. It provides solid footing on uneven terrain as well as excellent ankle support alignment for one who works on his feet all day.

Perfect fit but had to return. I think I'm getting tired of the High High Heals to wear at the office. These proved to be too uncomfortable by the end of the day.

I ordered a size 6 in a light nude leather. These are a perfect color for light skin tones especially with a neutral or cool undertone. I m about as standard as it gets in shoes, almost always a 6 unless the shoes don t run true to size. I would say these shoes are tighter in the toe box and slightly narrow throughout. Lastly, i noticed some reviews mentioned these possibly being a wide width because of the "W" next to the size mine say W 8 .... So hopefully I can clear up any confusion about that--so with the Crocs brand, many if not most of their styles are unisex- and they use the "W" for Women's sizing and in turn, use a "M" for Men's sizing. Also, typically if it's a wide width, the "W" will be after the size on the shoe, not before it, if that makes sense. So to be clear, these are definitely not wide width sizes. Order your true size, or size up of your a half size.

representative_reviews.text: I've had nothing but Merrell hiking boots since the late 1980s. They've always been rugged and well made until 2021. I had and old pair with hundred of miles and decided to retire them. I hike in Arizona where it's hot and the trails are rocky and rugged. Got the new pair I am evaluating and was shocked by its poor quality. Read what you may, the paper thin insert does not give an iota of support. So I purchased another makers supports which gave me the comfort I needed. Well, in the center of the heel area is a profound seam that at the 3. 5 mile mark of a six mile hike, I thought I had blisters. Nope not a blister, but rather a friction caused laceration of my left heel the right heel had the blister . What a disappointment that I had to go back to the paper thin insert. Shoe's wore out within 2 months so I purchased my first pair of Salomon boots x-crest . Merrell your R-D people should be required to wear those shoes as punishment.

Usually, I love Merrell Hiking boots. With my last pair I hiked the grand canyon three times! This pair has been a tremendous disappointment only because after 3 weeks of daily use as a K9 Handler the right boot inside toe started ripping, stitching is coming out and had to use Shoe Goo to repair them. These should come with Shoe Goo to repair the stitching. These are my most comfortable boots and truly waterproof. My last pair were half this price and lasted three years of hiking trips. Too bad they don't make the right boot as well as they do the left boot. I'm going to recommend they sell these boots separately. I know the issue is not width because these are wide. For Merrell boots I'd recommend going cheap if for daily wear, the more costly don't seem to equal better quality. For me these were a waste of money! They're great while they last - about two months - at this rate if I kept buying these Merrells new, it would cost me about 800 a year!

I purchased two pair, one I've been wearing for 3-4 months, the other is still new. I started feeling something odd a few weeks back, like my socks were bunching up under my toes, but no matter what I did I couldn't get the shoe to feel right. When I pull out the insoles and run my fingers along the soles inside the shoe, there's a big wave that's formed behind my toes and in front of the ball of my foot. Checking the new pair, that part of the sole is perfectly flat. SO the shoe's sole material seems to be migrating back from under my toes to the area in from of the ball of my foot. It isn't very comfortable and if it continues to get worse I'm going to see if this might be a warranty issue.

The boot itself was well made and did not require any break in. They did not cut off circulation or dig into the top of my feet. However, there were severe pressure points where the arch of my foot joins my heel. I inspected the shoe and found that the outermost lug on the outside is actually angled, and when bent, puts pressure on the exact part of my where the pain was located. I included a photo with the lug in question circled. If it wasn't for this issue I would have gladly given it 5 stars. But, because I had to return them for being unwearable, can not give a positive review.

Half of the rubber in the front of the shoe peeled off after my very first hike wearing these. I bought them after reading a review from NYT, which rated it highly, so this kind of poor quality is a surprise. The loose rubber in the front of the shoe may catch on things like roots on a hiking trail or let water seep in. This is unacceptable, especially for the premium price they charge. I had to return them.

Shoes make my nfeet, legs and back hurt. Spoke with someone at Merrell shoes. They said that they would take care of the situation. Replace shoes with another pair. HAVE NOT HEARD BACK FROM MERREL SHOES AT ALL!!!!

I have a pair of these I purchased a year ago from a sporting goods store. They proved to be very durable and comfortable but a bit on the small side. In those I had hiked well over 400 miles and perhaps worn 50 off the tread. Other than them being a bit small, fit and construction was stellar. I relegated them to the sports closet for summer time wear with thinner socks. Meanwhile, in late December 2018, I purchased a pair 1 2 size larger. The construction, fit and comfort was on par with the previous pair. Sadly. Very sadly, the durability was not. Seriously what happened!? I have 7 weeks of usage and maybe 100 miles on these! The treads are ripping off and over 50 of the tread wear life is gone. How can that be??? Merrell, what happened? I no longer feel trust in your product s nor can I afford to purchase boots every 3 months if I was so inclined. These say Vibram soles but are totally and completely without the legendary Vibram durability. Update I attempted to contact Merrell but received no response. A temporary solution to lug and sole separation is to re-attach using superglue. I'll do that for awhile to attempt to get my money's worth out of the purchase but will no longer buy any Merrell product.

These boots will make your foot issues much worse if you use them all day every day. My last pair went down on me in 7 weeks and that is intolerable! They were once a decent boot, but seem to be be more Chinese each time I order them. They will give you no cushion, no support and they are rigid. The strings will tighten up as the day goes on, giving your feet the feeling of being strangled. Not to worry Merrell, I will never be ordering another pair!

I ve owned four different types of Merrell shoes and boots and I ve always been satisfied. This pair is poorly designed and causes pain if worn for any length of time.

Two and a half years ago I broke my right foot, a massive lisfranc injury that put me down completely for several months. Since then I've been wearing some New Balance shoes with removable arch support. They have done a good job, but this summer I've decided to resume some hiking in the fabulous mountains here in Utah. I soon found that what worked well for my foot walking around town was not adequate for rocky trails in the mountains. After some research I picked these Merrell Moabs for my hiking adventures. My first adventure with them was a repeat of a recent hike using my New Balances. The Moabs were a very pleasant change. Note that most arch support inserts do great cushioning in the heel area, but provide almost no cushioning for the ball of the feet, which is where my foot pain occurs. I used two cheapo Scholls air cusion inserts in each show, which provided additional cushioning for the ball of the foot, although not gel padding. With those inserts in, the shoe fits perfectly, and my broken foot was no problem at all on a very rocky trail, going more than twice as far as the earlier problem hike. I'm sold on these Moabs!
Very comfortable so far and have used it for a week or use for walking with my dog in the woods, uphill, downhill, sideways, etc.
This is by far the most comfortable work boot I have ever owned. Also, if you are looking for the perfect hiking boot look no further!

These boots are amazing, and I think I'll be buying them again when these ones break down.

I figure if I get at least a year out of them, I'm doing alright. You may need to replace the insoles because the arch is fully supported and it's annoying IF you are "flat-footed".

I liked that this shoe fit snug around my feet. The waterproofing worked as expected, but I haven't yet tried standing in water for extended periods of time. I do wish there was more arch support for this though.

Love Merrill s for hiking. These boots are a great weight for the support they give. Keep your feet dry, and you can move easily up down trails w great arch and ankle support. They are a great diet color too!

Completely unacceptable to sell products in this condition.

Fit really narrow if you normally wear a normal width buy wide because mine fit tight in toe area should of bought at wide beside that beat boot on the market,light,waterproof and I wear boots five days a week for work
True to size. Arch support where it should be. I have a narrow foot so medium width is what I chose. Great shoe first time wear!
Wore them right out of the box, had to size up half a size. But, then they were perfect! Ready for my Iceland trip.

Well made by reputable Co. Going by size chart provided exact, very accurate. If you need to measure feet with cloth tape be sure you're standing up for length of foot when you do this. Toe is roomy cut for thicker trail socks than what I normally wear out in yard Wide width that I chose was perfect! Eyelets and ankle pull loop are sewn with Icey white day-glo so they light up in the dark! Vibram soles typically unmatched for positive traction Very comfortable already relieving sore foot stress
Great shoes, this is my second pair. Fitment seems true to size and very comfortable. Very functional.

Finally a hiking shoe that is wide in the toe box. This 2E size 9 is wider than many other name brands. Also lots of room in the instep for my high arches. Required no break-in time, they felt comfortable out of the box. Wore them for an entire weekend of camping immediately after receiving them. One night was raining steadily, while wearing a rain suit and walking around the campsite for hours, these kept my feet dry. Probably have about 10 miles on them so far, can't find any faults other than they can be a little hot in warmer weather.

I ordered a 12W and the toe box was higher, but not wider, and overall, not comfortable. Also, the insole on the left shoe felt uneven and bumpy, plus there is noisy, crinkly material waterproofing? in the uppers.
Snug fit with excellent support. I wish I would have gone with a half size larger. They are still doable.

Great hiking boot, wear this around everywhere. Fits true to size, it is a little tight narrow. Some reviews say it's not for anyone with a wide foot, I agree. Toe box and arch support are very good. Comfortable all day long.

These 11.5 wide merrells fit a little more snug than my previous set. Overall comfortable but maybe just need broke in. Old shoes lasted 3 years of use overseas in rough terrain. Durable and long lasting is why I ordered two more pair.
They fit perfect right out of the box! I have really wide feet and this almost never happens! Hiked in them several times! No soreness at all and I didn t even break them in slowly!
I have bought this exact same product, style, and size for the past 10 years every other year. Works great with a good fit.

I liked that this shoe fit snug around my feet. The waterproofing worked as expected, but I haven't yet tried standing in water for extended periods of time. I do wish there was more arch support for this though.
normally wear size 12. ordered these in size 13. fit great and very comfy. great for hiking or just walking around.

durability.issue_summary: 구매자들은 내구성 문제로 인해 신발이 빠르게 손상되거나 떨어져 나가는 경우가 많아 실망하고 있습니다.
durability.strength_summary: 구매자들은 이 신발이 내구성이 뛰어나고 오랜 사용에도 잘 견딘다고 반복적으로 언급하고 있습니다.

representative_reviews.text: I have a pair of these I purchased a year ago from a sporting goods store. They proved to be very durable and comfortable but a bit on the small side. In those I had hiked well over 400 miles and perhaps worn 50 off the tread. Other than them being a bit small, fit and construction was stellar. I relegated them to the sports closet for summer time wear with thinner socks. Meanwhile, in late December 2018, I purchased a pair 1 2 size larger. The construction, fit and comfort was on par with the previous pair. Sadly. Very sadly, the durability was not. Seriously what happened!? I have 7 weeks of usage and maybe 100 miles on these! The treads are ripping off and over 50 of the tread wear life is gone. How can that be??? Merrell, what happened? I no longer feel trust in your product s nor can I afford to purchase boots every 3 months if I was so inclined. These say Vibram soles but are totally and completely without the legendary Vibram durability. Update I attempted to contact Merrell but received no response. A temporary solution to lug and sole separation is to re-attach using superglue. I'll do that for awhile to attempt to get my money's worth out of the purchase but will no longer buy any Merrell product.
Before putting the boot on, the rivet attaching the metal hook eyelet pulled out of the fabric as I was lacing the boot for the 1st time.

I first gave it a 4 star raring. Only because there were some minor scuffs. Didn't really pay any mind. Received my purchase 12 13 2022. Not even a month later the toe separated. I went to super glue it and then noticed that, it looked like it had already been glued together just look at the photos I'm not happy at all. I paid 110 for these. And I reiterate yet again, it had to be second hand. I will be requesting a prompt refund. Hate to be this guy. But extremely displeased and disappointed with the overall outcome of this product.

Rubber sole on one boot fell off less than one month of use. Had to walk around for a couple hours with it flopping around until I was dobe with work. Looked like bad glue job but I can't say for sure. My previous Merrells lasted 2 years before they developed a small hole now I am back to wearing them wearing them and avoiding puddles.

2 days after the end of the return date, and after my 6th time wearing them, the top lace came off... Getting a replacement is ridiculously aggravating ... Especially when they don't answer tour emails !!
Shoes did not hold up, soles fell off without even getting worn out. Lace loop broke. Stitching fell out. Merrell is going down hill

The stitching on the side of the left boot is already coming apart after less than a month. Really disappointing because they were decent boots otherwise. I'm sure it's only a matter of time before the stitching on the right boot starts to come undone as well.

The boot itself was well made and did not require any break in. They did not cut off circulation or dig into the top of my feet. However, there were severe pressure points where the arch of my foot joins my heel. I inspected the shoe and found that the outermost lug on the outside is actually angled, and when bent, puts pressure on the exact part of my where the pain was located. I included a photo with the lug in question circled. If it wasn't for this issue I would have gladly given it 5 stars. But, because I had to return them for being unwearable, can not give a positive review.

I initially left a 4 star review see below . About a month after I wrote that review, the heel of the Vibram sole began to separate from the leather of the boot. When I contacted support, they claim that they can't replace the boot with the same Beluga color that I originally ordered, although their website shows that it is indeed in-stock. For replacements, they asked for photos, and then they wanted me to cut a gash down the side of the boots that I have in hand before they will send me replacements of another color. As if the separating sole isn't enough evidence that they bad. Not so happy about this any more. What if after I cut a gash in the boot, then they decide not to send a replacement pair. Any judge would say, "Oh, you intentionally inflicted damage to the boot? Too bad, so sad..." Has anyone ever done this before? In the pictures, it appears that the adhesive is only sticking to the black part of the sole, and not to the grey leather. Is this going to happen to another pair if I do get a replacement? I did finally receive a new pair a Beluga colored boots, as I originally ordered. This winter 2020-2021 we were hiking in the snow. The tread isn't as aggressive and doesn't stick to the snow and ice like my previous pair of Merrell boots. My feet did stay warm with just a single pair of wool socks. I like that the boots breathe and moisture can evaporate out. Even in hot weather, my boots weren't soaked from sweat. I've only stepped in a few shallow puddles, so I haven't put the boots to the water-proof test much. The previous pair had Gortex, which lasted several years before I simply wore the boots out. I don't think that the Moab pair will last as well as the previous pair. I wish Merrell still had the previous style available. My original review I like the fit of this boot around my foot. I'd like a little more padding in the heal. I have owned a previous pair and style of Merrill boots that had Cordura fabric that came all the way up both sides of the tongue that prevented any water, gravel, weeds, and grass seeds from entering my boot. This particular boot doesn't have the full height fabric by the tongue, but does come up part way. Now that winter is here, my boots are comfortable with wool socks, even in the cold air, so I'm looking forward to putting them to the test this winter and all through next summer of hiking and backpacking. They seem to have good construction and built to last. I hope they last as many years as my previous pair, which lasted for almost 3 years before they started to wear out, leak and lose tread. I trust the Merrill name for boots. Update 7 29 21 The replacement pair of boots that Merrell sent me were not waterproof, as stated. The toe of my right boot dipped below the surface of the water as I crossed a small steam, and I immediately felt water inside of my boot. It felt like it was just any normal pair of boots with no waterproofing. Because this was the replacement pair, Merrill won t replace this pair. They had me destroy the first pair, so I still don t have a good, solid, working-as-claimed pair of boots. They only offered me 30 discount on another pair. No thank you. I ll buy quality next time. What happened to the Merrill quality I experienced back in 95? Go Salomon next time.

Very disappointed in the quality of the sewn-in shoelace eyelets. I only wore these four times and the fifth time I put them on and started lacing them up the shoelace eyelet tore right out of the boot. You can see the torn off eyelet and where it tore out in my picture. I only wore them for hikes on the unimproved path in our local park system so they weren't even out in tough trail conditions. Unfortunately, it happened after the 30 day return window. All Amazon could do was offer a return and I would be charged a 20 "restocking" fee. There's nothing to restock seeing as the product is defective and is now worthless. I also called the seller Orva Stores and left a voicemail but never heard back. I read the reviews and saw they were mainly positive and was between these and another brand. Guess I'll go with the other brand from a different seller for my replacement pair.

It says "waterproof" but the bottoms of my feet socks got wet, at the first havy rain I faced hiking with it. Regular expected usage and no structural damage happened. Want to return replace but do not see option at Amazon. It was brought 5 months ago. Fits perfectly, "rides" perfectly, but did not hold the promise of waterproofing.

I've had nothing but Merrell hiking boots since the late 1980s. They've always been rugged and well made until 2021. I had and old pair with hundred of miles and decided to retire them. I hike in Arizona where it's hot and the trails are rocky and rugged. Got the new pair I am evaluating and was shocked by its poor quality. Read what you may, the paper thin insert does not give an iota of support. So I purchased another makers supports which gave me the comfort I needed. Well, in the center of the heel area is a profound seam that at the 3. 5 mile mark of a six mile hike, I thought I had blisters. Nope not a blister, but rather a friction caused laceration of my left heel the right heel had the blister . What a disappointment that I had to go back to the paper thin insert. Shoe's wore out within 2 months so I purchased my first pair of Salomon boots x-crest . Merrell your R-D people should be required to wear those shoes as punishment.
Bought theses 10 months ago as a back up I love Merrell MOAB fit . Just broke them out a week ago, today I walked in heavy rain and toes leaked. Of course it's too late to return them.
Not happy at all thought they would last for the money I spent on them! Got these boots in March and they are falling apart already

UPDATED REVIEW received a defective pair and Merrell replaced them. Cool. 3 weeks later, the sole comes unglued. Not cool. I'm not even asking for a replacement as the product is not fit to be worn. They fall apart see pic , they were NOT waterproof even before the sole failed, and this is the second failed pair in a row. Merrell, once a good brand, is now owned by Wolverine. Wolverine is widely known for making cheap boots for cheap people using cheap labor in Vietnam. There's an executive somewhere spending the money they saved on glue... he should be tossed into the sarlacc.
Great boots I use for work my last pair lasted 3 years and wore at least 5 days week. In all conditions.

Cheap hard plastic insert instead of a foam foot insole. I took the foam insoles out of an old pair of Sketchers and put them in the Merrells and they are fantastic. If you buy a pair of these get some Dr. Scholl inserts or take some out of another pair of shoes and you will love them. I use mine for hiking everyday and they are comfortable, Grip and wear well and are waterproof. Merrell ought to be ashamed for making such an uncomfortable shoe to save a few pennies on foam. Sketchers at a quarter the price feel better on your feet.

Well made by reputable Co. Going by size chart provided exact, very accurate. If you need to measure feet with cloth tape be sure you're standing up for length of foot when you do this. Toe is roomy cut for thicker trail socks than what I normally wear out in yard Wide width that I chose was perfect! Eyelets and ankle pull loop are sewn with Icey white day-glo so they light up in the dark! Vibram soles typically unmatched for positive traction Very comfortable already relieving sore foot stress
Great for hiking, immediately comfortable. Affordable and no need for a breaking in period. Sturdy construction, should last for years.

These shoes saved a foot leg of Ukrainian soldier. Several pieces of artillery stuck in the sole with only one small piece going through. Soldier was able to fully recover from his injury and going back to the frontline in 1.5 weeks. I sent him a new pair of these. He says they are most comfortable and durable shoes.

Merrill is always high quality, and look just like the picture, fit nice right out of the box with no break in period. Either buy them for work or play but not both, once they get dirty there isn t much you can do. There not really washable as it lightens the color of the suede but I would have no other, they are warm in winter and dry. Enjoy.

My second pair of these after wearing out the first set, comfy, require very little break in, have not ventured out in heavy rain yet. Thanks Amazon for offering choice that we don't always get in Oz.

Nothing's perfect. So when I tell you these are "ok", it means they are better then expected, and good enough for me. BUT, adjust your expectations, because so much of what is sold today is absolute CRAP. So these are significantly better then CRAP, but who knows for how long ? I figure if I get at least a year out of them, I'm doing alright. You may need to replace the insoles because the arch is fully supported and it's annoying IF you are "flat-footed".

I love these shoes! This not the first time I have purchased them and won t be the last. I play a lot of disc golf and put a lot of miles in these shoes and deal with all kinds of weather. Best shoe on the market for the out doors.

The first pair of Merrell s I ever owned was way back when the company was in the US. They lasted more than 20 years which included tramping around in the jungles of Central America. The inside finally rotted out. They ve received a lot of bad press since then regarding shoddy construction. I don t travel anymore and haven t put very many miles on these but so far so good. I ll update in another six months.
I have bought this exact same product, style, and size for the past 10 years every other year. Works great with a good fit.

This is one of the better good-but-not-great quality boots I've tried. Only about 25 miles on them so far with a very light pack, but the soles are reasonably sticky for mild rock scrambles and the mid-rise provides some, albeit not great, ankle support. The fuller rubber toe cap should help these hold up over time, and they were reasonably snug on steep downhills. I wish i could get the top to cinch a bit tighter near the ankle though. The tongue is also weirdly puffy for some reason. I haven't tried the waterproofing, and am a little skeptical when mesh claims to also be waterproof, but it seems multilayered enough that maybe it's possible. The biggest surprise to me was how much better the balance is on these, compared to the low-top. The low-top version feels heavy and a little clunky to me, but I didn't notice the same feeling with the mid.

These boots fit great and the uppers wear very well. My issue is with the soles. Vibram is supposed to be a superior wear product and on these boots, it just isn t. I have three pairs in different colors. The beluga color soles wore fine and after 2 years of FedEx delivering, which means hard use, they started to show wear - see pic. The Graphite and black pairs I got wore down to almost zero traction in less than a year each. So, either Merrell is turning out crap products all of a sudden or these are inferior Chinese clones. Whatever the case, no matter how much I love all the other aspects of these boots, they are not worth the cost if the soles can t stand up any more. And yes, I wear inserts to help reduce that wear for those questioning The color on the Graphite model also faded to a tan and looks almost identical to the Beluga ones.
I've been buying this hiking boot for the past 6 years because it fits my feet perfectly, has great traction, and is durable.

This things can take a massive beating. Had em a year now, only shoes I wear, often walk 5 miles home from work for the fresh air and these HOLD UP. Last pair I had actually was about dead around the one year mark, which is odd, but my current pair is better than I had hoped. Order them a half size larger than normal I suggest, they're too small if you don't.

design.strength_summary: 구매자들은 다양한 색상과 뛰어난 착용감을 강조하며 디자인에 대한 긍정적인 반응을 보이고 있습니다.
