price.issue_summary: 가격에 비해 품질이 매우 낮아 소비자들이 실망하고 있습니다. 많은 구매자들이 이 제품이 가치가 없다고 느끼고 있습니다.
price.strength_summary: 고객들은 가격 대비 뛰어난 가치를 강조하며, 합리적인 가격으로 만족스러운 구매 경험을 하고 있습니다.

representative_reviews.text: Garbage! For 120.00 they are complete trash! I have had these for less than a year, and the soles are falling off. I have bought better from Walmart for less than 25.00! The quality is completely sub par! Do not waste your money on these! I would demand a refund, but but these pieces of junk aren't worth the effort..

Owned a pair of moabs years ago, that's why I bought these. As I'm wearing them I sort of regret my purchase. I don't think that they're made quite as well as they used to be. Variations in the leather make me think it's just pure poor quality. I'll have to see how the seams stand up but I won't pay this much money for Merrells anymore.
Great for the price. My third pair over 8 years. First bought for a hike in upper Utah and was perfect support and comforf.
This is a great shoe for the price. Only thing I didn t like was the inserts, but that s really a personal choice for me and probably most people.
Bought the Merrel MOAB 3 for a trip to the Blue Ridge Mountains. Exceeded my expectations. Comfortable and durable.
Great product in Merrell s finest tradition at a reasonable price. The only con for me, I wish they were smooth leather instead of short nap suede.

I love these shoes! This not the first time I have purchased them and won t be the last. I play a lot of disc golf and put a lot of miles in these shoes and deal with all kinds of weather. Best shoe on the market for the out doors.
Great for hiking, immediately comfortable. Affordable and no need for a breaking in period. Sturdy construction, should last for years.
I love these hiking boots. I wished that I would have paid a little more and bought them to begin with instead of cheaper ones.

product_name: Clarks Women's Annadel Eirwyn Wedge Sandal

urgent_issues.summary: 많은 고객들이 사이즈가 작고 좁아서 불만을 토로하고 있습니다. 이로 인해 불편함을 겪고 있으며, 반품 기한을 놓치는 경우도 발생하고 있습니다.

comfort.issue_summary: 구매자들은 착용감이 불편하고 통증을 유발하는 문제를 반복적으로 경험하고 있습니다. 이로 인해 많은 고객들이 신발을 반품하게 되었습니다.
comfort.strength_summary: 구매자들은 이 신발이 착용감이 뛰어나고 하루 종일 신어도 불편함이 없다고 반복적으로 언급하고 있습니다. 편안한 착용감 덕분에 다양한 상황에서 즐겁게 신을 수 있습니다.

representative_reviews.text: I have Plantar Fasciitis heel pain . First I had it in my right heel now in the left. I have two pairs of Clarks wedges the beige Aisley Tulip see picture and black Annadel Fareda. I can wear them ALL day, without pains in my heel or else. BEST most Comfortable wedges EVER. Now I had ordered the Black Annadel Eirwyn, and this shoes does NOT fit my feet as comfy as my other two Clark wedges. the foot bed is narrow. I post pictures comparing the new black Annadel Eirwyn to my beige Aisley Tulip. both shoes are the same size. But you can see how my heel hangs over on the new black Annadel Eirwyn. I am surprised about the different size foot bed. It is still very soft, but not as comfortable because of being so narrow. They run a little small too for me. Had to order one size up. I will wear them at home for a day or two to see if my feet adjust, when not I have to send them back.

I own these in navy and thought it would be nice to have a pair in white, these feel much smaller, I thought they would stretch out but the first time I wore them ended up with severe blisters on both ankles from the strap rubbing. VERY DISAPPOINTED
Something is wrong with this shoe. The shoe is like a whole size reduced in size, the foot sticks out from behind. Don t waste your time..

I love Clark s. I ve been a long time buyer due to foot problems. This brand typically delivers stylish, comfortable and versatile shoes. Not this time. These shoes were INCREDIBLY uncomfortable. Painful. I got 3 blisters between both my feet. This has NEVER happened to me with Clark shoes. I m so saddened because they re absolutely stunning. Gorgeous shoes. I m very upset by the quality. I m going to buy inserts and see what I can do to make them work. But if you re tossed up between getting them or not and you suffer from feet problems. There are better shoes from this brand to spend your money on. I wouldn t buy these shoes again

These sandals are very comfortable however my feet smell in them. I HAVE NEVER had stinky feet but these shoes make my feet smell like my teen boys feet. I ve worn many many shoes similar to these but has never been an issues. Maybe the material makes feet sweat more? Idk. Whatever it is I hate them!
Bought the same shoe from the same vendor in a different color and they were perfect. However, the black ones are tight and blistered my feet. Very upset I missed the return window by 1 day.
Sent back, way too small even though I sized up. Also extremely narrow and I do not have a wide foot. I wants these to work soo bad.
These look good but the metal buckle cuts right into the ankle bone and sends a shot of pain into the bone every time you walk. Not good .

Weird fit and very uncomfortable foot bed, felt like I was walking on a block... not smooth like the insole looks. I thought size was off, so I tried a size up but hey were then too big, but still had the weird foot bed thing. I returned and bought a sister shoe from sketchers which I rated 5 Stars for comfort and fit.
The fit was too narrow. I wear a size 9.5 or 10. I ordered these navy sandals in a size 10, I had plenty of room but it left my arch hurting walking small distances and standing.

On the left shoe the Velcro makes it unwearable. Part of the Velcro came through on the stitches so it digs into my ankle. Then the Velcro isn t lined up on the side. Final Velcro issue on the left, it sounds like the Velcro is coming off as I walk. Finally, not delivered on time!!

These are so cute but unfortunately my feet slide down through the toe area and they keep sliding to the side. I m constantly stopping to straighten my foot in them. It s not because they re too big as the length is a bit short. When I first put them on they re a perfect fit.

EDIT I am now editing my review for this product. I have been in love with these shoes since I started wearing them! They have form fitted to my feet and are so very comfortable! I take excellent care of them. The bottoms of the shoes are not worn at all. However, around month 3, the shoes have started to come apart. The platform is separating from the footbed and straps on both shoes. My return window has expired for the shoes, and I have not been able to contact the seller. I did send an email to Clarks, and got a response. I emailed back pictures of the defective areas, along with a proof of purchase. Clarks is willing to inspect the shoes and if they decide that the shoes are defective, then they will send a replacement. If not, the shoes will be destroyed. I will also be responsible for all shipping. Considering that I will spend almost 20 in shipping costs, and I only spent 40 on the shoes in the first place, I will am not willing to take the gamble with Clarks. If there was some way to contact the seller, that would be my best bet. I hope that by changing my review from 5 stars to 2 stars can help me remedy my issue. I followed the other reviews that suggested that these shoes would run small, so I ordered the appropriate size. These shoes are very comfortable to wear all day while at work. I do not walk very much in them, but they are comfortable. I love the color because they work with most any colors for spring summer.
Disappointed! Clarks quality is taking a plunge. Second try for the same white sandals. Have to return this one too. Velcro on the sandal is poorly placed and hurts the foot. Will try another brand.

On the plus side, it's hard to find shoes that are comfortable for my 10W foot and these are wide enough. However, manufacturers must think if you have a large, wide foot that the rest of you must be large and wide. Not true. I have a narrow heel and narrow ankles. The back strap on these are too loose and they're designed so you can't punch an additional hole to make them tighter. The insole is soft and cushy. However, the heel is hard and too thin! and clacks loudly when you walk. I'm not sure if I'm going to keep these.

Beautiful sandals but much higher than I expected. I was looking for sandals I could wear comfortably to commute to work and home on a weekly basis. These are sandals that can be dressed up or worn for light leisurely walks. They are high and the heel is not as soft as the front. It seems to have a bit of arch support. I am keeping them because I was able to get them for less than half the price with an amazon reward and they will be useful to dress up or for light walking. They are not for trekking on trains. I have a pair from another brand that seems to be out of commission that was less high up and so comfortable for walking an entire day and on my feet, those are showing wear and tear and I was hoping these were similar. Guess not.
I can wear it all day without any discomfort! Very comfortable, goes with everything because of the nude color, can't wait for summer again, so I can wear it all the time!
Very comfortable, fits true to size, and wide width is so nice to have! Easy to walk and stand in for long periods of time!
Upper leather very soft, the review helped me a lot I buy one size up supposed to be size 6, I got size 7 fit me so good, I can walk eight hours at work with no problem
Good features with velcro fastener on heel allows me to adjust to my perfect fit. Footbed is awesome and comfortable!

I always have pain in my heals Clark shoes is a brand that works well for me. This is my 1st pair of Clark heals they are really comfortable. Platform heal makes them almost feel like your in flats.Fit is true to size. I could wear these all day. Looks great with any outfit .
Last minute I needed some comfy wedges! These came through, didn t need to break them in and I wore them all day and night! New favorite wedges!

These are exactly what I was looking for comfortable, neutral summer wedge that I can wear with everything. The leather is so soft and breathable. The soles are really nice and sturdy. These shoes are very comfortable to walk in. I got the Nude color and it's perfect for me.

The perfect shoe! These shoes are extremely comfortable. I've walked miles in these and took them on vacation with me. Absolutely no pain whatsoever! Definitely buy these if you're looking for a cute, comfortable shoe!

I researched and read a ton of reviews for various comfortable but cute sandals wedges. I was going to a conference, where I d be on my feet for hours, with tons of walking. I don t have the greatest back, so support is important as well. These are a winner. These are so buttery soft the moment you put them on. Zero break-in time. Just slide them on and go. They are supportive and fit like a glove. I wore them the rest of the summer, received compliments on them, and am very happy with these!
So comfortable. Literally can have these on all day and I don t get tired at all. They look great and I always get compliments. It s like wearing heals without wearing heals. I love it!

Have older problematic feet.. bad bunions curling toes that one surgeon wanted 40,000 to fix! The 2nd surgeon told me to try using yoga toe spacers each night while I use a heated roller-ball foot massager while watching tv AND change my shoe types brands to wider versions less heel, which I quickly did tuhduh I m still happily walk n!! Now I had ordered the Black Annadel Eirwyn, and this shoes does NOT fit my feet as comfy as my other two Clark wedges. the foot bed is narrow. I post pictures comparing the new black Annadel Eirwyn to my beige Aisley Tulip. both shoes are the same size. But you can see how my heel hangs over on the new black Annadel Eirwyn. I am surprised about the different size foot bed. It is still very soft, but not as comfortable because of being so narrow. They run a little small too for me. Had to order one size up. I will wear them at home for a day or two to see if my feet adjust, when not I have to send them back.

These are very cute BUT - they run small! I did not really believe the other reviews. I wear a size 7 Narrow, but just barely some 7's are a little too long for me, so I figured a 7 on the short side would be perfect . These 7's were somewhere in between a 6.5 a 7. I also wear a Narrow and these were good snug. There was a nice cushion in the heel. But I am sending back because they are too short in length they felt very unstable - my foot wobbled side to side I am a pretty experienced high heel wearer, but these are more narrow on the bottom surface than at the foot bed .

On the plus side, it's hard to find shoes that are comfortable for my 10W foot and these are wide enough. The back strap on these are too loose and they're designed so you can't punch an additional hole to make them tighter. The insole is soft and cushy. Good features with velcro fastener on heel allows me to adjust to my perfect fit. Footbed is awesome and comfortable!

The shoe feels snug at first, in the toe area, but the leather is very soft, the sole of the foot has great support, and you can walk in these forever. The good part is, it looks like a normal wedge. EDIT I am now editing my review for this product. I have been in love with these shoes since I started wearing them! They have form fitted to my feet and are so very comfortable! I take excellent care of them. The bottoms of the shoes are not worn at all. However, around month 3, the shoes have started to come apart. The platform is separating from the footbed and straps on both shoes. My return window has expired for the shoes, and I have not been able to contact the seller. I did send an email to Clarks, and got a response. I emailed back pictures of the defective areas, along with a proof of purchase. Clarks is willing to inspect the shoes and if they decide that the shoes are defective, then they will send a replacement. If not, the shoes will be destroyed. I will also be responsible for all shipping. Considering that I will spend almost 20 in shipping costs, and I only spent 40 on the shoes in the first place, I will am not willing to take the gamble with Clarks. If there was some way to contact the seller, that would be my best bet. I hope that by changing my review from 5 stars to 2 stars can help me remedy my issue. I needed a pair of dress shoes for church, and I really had a hard time finding a pair in black, that were comfortable enough to wear while dealing with the heel pain of plantar fasciitis. I read the reviews on these shoes and decided to give them a try and I am so glad I did! I am a firm size 7 and these fit me to a tee. I'm short and appreciate higher heels, but I can't tolerate shoes with high heels unless they are a platform style, like these. The black material is a faux suede and it does stretch slightly, which adds to the comfort. There is a strap that Velcro's behind the heel, and I like the ability to adjust it to a tighter or looser fit. Although the heels are 3", they are super comfortable to wear! I wore these for 4 hours today, with more than half of that time being on my feet, and I could have gone many more hours in these shoes. Extremely comfortable. They are SUPER light weight, and I did find myself stubbing my toes on carpet - probably because I am not used to wearing such high heels and the fact that they are so lightweight. I soon got used to this however, and it's not an issue. The insole is nicely padded and provides the quality that I have come to expect from Clark's shoes. The bottoms are not slippery at all, and should be good this winter if there is any snow or ice in my path to church. I really don't have anything negative to say about these shoes, other than the fact that I have to be careful when putting them on if I am wearing nylons, because the Velcro can easily catch on nylons and put a run in them - but any shoe with a Velcro closure can cause this to occur. Still, I would rather have Velcro than a buckle any day. I think these are a terrific value.

representative_reviews.text: i don't know what has happened to keen. i've been wearing their sandals since 2006 and this latest pair i ordered was complete junk. they fit way too tight and were very stiff. this is my fourth pair of keen newports in the same size, so i know exactly how they should fit. these were just wrong. i should also note, my first pair of keens lasted about eight years and were amazing. they saw many destinations around the world. i retired them when the sole started separating in the back. my second pair only lasted a couple years and the sole of both completely delaminated and fell apart. even though the construction was seemingly on a downward trend, i ordered this replacement pair. i returned them immediately. if you still want keen sandals, consider trying their american made versions. i ended up with the rialto sandals. they don't fit quite as wide as my old newports, but they don't squeeze my feet or prevent splay either. the different feel took some getting used to, but they are much higher quality overall. they do have an insole that soaks up water and squishes as you walk, but it's not terrible and they still dry faster than a pair of shoes would.

I really want to like these but was hoping I could wear them without socks. The stitching on the side is extremely rough and causes blisters on the top and side of your foot from the rubbing on the rough fabric. Wearing these with socks is awesome but who wants to wear socks with these?

Very comfortable for a sandal water shoe. After walking several miles, feet showed no sign of soreness or blisters. Shoes seems very well made. Big issue is that the soles are slippery when wet which is a problem for water shoes. Super slippers on wet rocks or wet floors. Other than that, I would have went 5 stars. Will try something else next time due to the slipperiness.
I love Keen shoes, but the is too shallow and my little toe rub to the point is gets a huge blister. It could use a larger toe box or a velcro heel strap like TEVA to tighten shoe.
Impossible to get them on!! Once on they fit ok. But there is no heal strap to unbuckle... making it virtually impossible to put on your feet. Poor design

When I noticed these on a friend I commented how durable they looked and he mentioned they were comfortable for recreational summer use. I purchased these and loved them for hiking and water shoes for my first few April and May hikes, but soon I noticed a metal staple in the foot bed that was causing pain as it pushed the sole slightly higher in that point. I tried to use pliers to push it down but could not repair them. The metal pin or staple was bent sideways enough to not move or change the form of the foot pad. Blisters always followed in that area if I wore them more than a few hours. After that I used them as shower shoes only at the gym. If that is what you are looking for, they do that well for the low price of 100. Yes, as others mentioned the stitching was falling apart after my brief activity but it was the defect that caused me to not use them for longer periods of time. My guess is the stitching would have eventuallu made them useless after one season with active use. I will say though that the shoe without defect issues was comfortable and I liked the design and color options. If this shoe was built to last like Teva and Merrell it could really be something. Hopefully others have had better experiences as I still think they look good and could work if better quality and craftsmanship. Unfortunately they seem to be making a cheap shoe that appears well made after pocketing the savings made on knock off quality sandals. No one will be using these in 2-3 years and 100 is not the right price for a 15-25 sandal you could easily buy at your local superstore.

I have normally-proportioned size 14 feet. I could not even get my feet into these. Most manufacturer's normal size 14 shoes Nike, Brooks, New Balance, etc. fit just fine well, to be honest, Nike's run pretty narrow in general . Not these. I understand they need to be snug, but it took 5 minutes just to get one on, and then it was so tight on my foot that I was afraid it would cut off the circulation. It's not the soul or last of the shoe which is the problem, but the webbing material. It is very tight over the top of your foot--tight enough to be very uncomfortable in my case. Returned.
What a disappointment. they charge you an extra 30 to have Jerry's name on it. Then send you undersized shoes. My foot would not even fit into it. Then they charge you 6 to send back.
These sandals are awesome except they wear the skin off my foot in one spot whenever I take them for a walk.

I have bought many Keen sandals but never have the interior been so stiff and hard on my feet. Perhaps if I can manage to wear them with socks comfortably in the winter it might compensate but I can't say that I would recommend this to anybody. Everything else about it's fine but if your feet hurt and a sandal well that's the end of the story
After used for 2 holidays altogether 20 days, saddlly the sandal was broken. both side of strap are coming off. I did not walk that much and did not use rough. I am surprised.

Upon receipt the sandals had dried glue on different areas of the sandals. Some of the straps had glue that looked like was coming undone. I do not know if the sandal was subject to heat prior to shipping that caused glue on this product to melt or if it was poor manufacturing. For a hundred dollars I expect higher quality. I'm returning the sandals and ordering a second pair. I'll update this review upon receipt of the new pair.

Either Keen changed their design since last summer or Amazon started selling a shiz product because these are NOT the same as what we bought last year. We bought the exact same size and model. Last year we hiked 6 miles in steady rain on the White Mountains and hundreds of miles throughout the summer. Zero breaking on. Great support. Our feet felt amazing. We purchased these to replace that pair that we'd worn out and they're horrible. Cause plantar fascitis, pain in calves and bottom side of foot, rubs at the back. Wth? And of course now we're past the ability to return and stuck with these terrible shoes we can't wear.

I purchased my first pair of Keen sandals about two years ago, and then pretty much proceeded to live in them for the next two years. My wife got after me to buy a new pair because my original pair was looking rather ragged. The design of these sandals has changed quite a bit, and it may not be obvious to you from the photos that are provided. The toe box has become substantially wider. This is great if you have a wide foot, but not so great if you don't. In the older version, there was a smallish black rubber front to the shoe. This has also gotten much larger and prominent, and quite honestly, it looks pretty ugly now. It is perhaps less noticeable if you get a model that is in black, but even on a dark blue model you now notice the front rubber immediately. I don't know who redesigned the shoe, but if I were assigning a grade, it would be a solid D-. I am going to keep these, but will be looking at similar products from other manufacturers. As soon as I find something that is a bit closer to the old design, this pair is unlikely to see the light of day. Very sad when you have a product that you really liked the design of, you buy it again, and then you find out that it now a very unattractive shoe. If they stick with this design, I certainly won't be buying it again. Needless to say, this was a disappointment. As scruffy as the old pair looks, I think they still look better than this new pair.

I have worn keen mens sandals for years. I am woman with wide feet. My feet always feel good in keen footwear. I worked in factories with cement floor for 30 some years. But there is something different about these. They have a chemical odor. The opening for the foot to go thru is smaller and there is no give to the material. They are the right size and are comfortable to wear once you get them on. But really hard to get on and still smell funny. I'm sure Keen new and improved them with cheaper material or outsource them or something. It's a shame. Have loved these shoes for years.

I love these shoes. They have a comfortable arch support. The tie system is easy. They have a good grip on multiple surfaces. They start out a little tight but quickly stretch to a comfortable size. I typically wear them hiking and they are great on all terrain. Sometimes dirt or little pebbles get caught inside but it s to be expected with any sandal
This order came in time for our trip to Costa Rica. Y husband loved the support, especially walking in wet terrain.

I think the soles of these hiking sandals are just too hard for us older gentlemen... I m 62, and pretty active. I work from home so I can exercise every morning, and every afternoon alternate between walking 1.25 miles on pavement and swimming 3 4 miles. The first time I walked the 1.25 miles in these sandals I got a hot spot on the outside of my right little toe. No problem... my bad... I should have worn socks the first long walk to stretch these out a little and smooth any rough spots. The next two 1.25 mile walks I wore socks, and 15-20 miles later, the hot spot has not came back. But, also the first 1.25 mile walk I had a very sore arch in my left foot and both hip joints were sore. I tried different walking styles and wore the sandals around the house to get them broken in. Well, after 15-20 miles, I ve decided that the soles are just too hard. I think the hard soles make me pound my feet down when I walk, which is causing the sore hips. This has also pulled that tendon in the arch of my left foot. And, neither pain is going away completely... the pain is slightly better, but not enough. I don t think I have weird feet, or am prone to foot walking issues. I normally wear Merrell s and also wear Teva and Sperry sandals, so I can handle arches or no arches just fine. I ve heard that as we age we lose fat padding in our hands and feet. I think that lack of natural padding and these hard soles are just a bad combination. So, if you re approaching gray beard age, these might not be the best choice. My wife really likes hers, but she hasn t walked as far as I have yet. I thought about adding an insert for padding, but with the somewhat open heel, I thought the insert might shift around too much. So, I just finished my first 1.25 mile walk in a pair of Teva Omnium 2 Sport Sandals. They are new and I wore socks. The Teva s have a noticeably softer sole... not spongy, but just soft enough for my old feet. Not only did my hips do just fine, but the arch tendon feels just as good as when I started the walk. I think I ll have to early retire the Keen s. Other than the hard sole of the Keen s Both the Teva s and the Keen s are great looking and feeling hiking sandals. We wanted hiking sandals for an upcoming active trip to Costa Rica. Either of these are perfect for that type of trip IMHO. I wore the Keen s on a kayaking outing last weekend. Had to carry the kayak over wet rocks a bit and the Keen s were great... they had solid grip and I didn t feel the rocks through the soles. The next morning they weren't quite dry, but close. They re a little hard to get on, but you quickly get used to pulling that back strap really hard to get them over your heel. They fit snug which is what you want for hiking up and down hills. So, wear socks the first mile or so... and if it feels like you re pounding your feet down when you walk, these Keen soles are probably too hard for you as well.
hiking at the narrow Zion national park and angel landing with this shoe .... work GREAT !!!! and very comfortable

Bought these as a gift for my husband who loves his Keen hiking boots so much that he bought a back-up pair of Keen boots. This is saying a lot because he's a forester, is in some kind of boot most of the time, and has tried them all. He has hard feet to size footwear for, as they're wide and also flat. Since this Keen brand seemed to work so well for him, I ordered 2 variations of these sandals as well as 2 sizes of each as a bday gift, so he'd be able to choose the best fit. The other Keen sandal I ordered was the original Keen sandal. I thought the older original and sized up would probably be the best fit for him best based on reviews I'd read, but it was these lighter lower profile sandals in his actual size not the sized up pair that fit him spot on!. A perfect match! And, with their lighter design, they looked way better on him than the heavier Keens. So happy these worked out -- they look great not too hulkish , and he loves them! A Plus is that these sandals ventilate well, and also cover up his bruised up toenails that he gets from year round field work on steep terrain in cleated hiking boots.

Super comfortable! Took them through hell and hell at Oaxaca beaches and mountains. Even treaded Mexico city with them. I use no more shoes today. I use them 25 7 not 24 7. I'm saving in socks and softener. But the price to pay is cheesy smelly feet.
We are planning a trip to Central America that will involve some wet conditions and these shoes look like they will dry quickly. I've had Keen's before and they give me great arch support.
Outstanding! My wife and I hiked over 10 miles and these shoes provided excellent traction and comfort! Wish I wold have had these 10 years ago! Highly recommend these shoes for water and hiking!

This sandal is reasonably comfortable and fits well. However, with my planar fascitis, the sole leaves something to be desired. The arch support is not as good as on the Keen Arroyo II, and the part of the sole facing the foot is not as soft. Overall, fits OK, works OK. But it should really be better, for the price.
The support straps over the top of the foot and at the heel are more comfortable than other sandals I've owned. I can wear these all day without an issue. They look nice as well.
Husband has assorted foot ankle issues..good coverage for toes ,good support,can get wet.Just what he needed.
Been wearing Keen s for 15 years , due to my wide feet and high arches . They are the ONLY shoes I ve found that are comfortable all day !

Bought these for my husband who'd had big toe surgery, because he needed a wide toe box. He normally wears 12, and I bought 13, not knowing how much extra room to get.These are a perfect fit with a good arch support, modest cupped heel and plenty of toe room with fully adjustable top lacing to keep the shoes from being loose to prevent rubbing blisters . He loves them!! I've always loved Keens because I have 34 paddle feet' 34 with a low arch. Now he's sold on the fit for his narrower feet with a high arch. P.S. He has complete neuropathy. So I check his feet often. He wears these almost every day, and there's no redness, blistering, swelling or lace rash marks. We find these are better than leather sandals recommended by his podiatrist from E e B r, Mer l, and R p rt.

I was asked by more than a few other guests who looked like they wish they had a pair walking with their feet directly on the rocks what I had on. There are comfortable and versatile and I am quite happy with the purchase. They already more than paid for what they cost on one nice trip to the hot springs!

I really don't like wearing shoes or boots so I was pleased to find some hiking sandals that are fairly breathable and minimal in design that I can take on longer hikes. So far I've hiked only a cumalative 9 miles or so but they've been comfortable and haven't given me any issues. The one downside is that little pebbles will get stuck under your foot and you sometimes have to stop and remove the sandals to let them out. A small price to pay for the freedom of not wearing boots though. Another thing that I haven't had any issue with but could see being a potential problem is there is of course no ankle support on sandals. It's just a fact, not a con. It's worth the risk to me.

representative_reviews.text: i don't know what has happened to keen. i've been wearing their sandals since 2006 and this latest pair i ordered was complete junk. they fit way too tight and were very stiff. this is my fourth pair of keen newports in the same size, so i know exactly how they should fit. these were just wrong. i should also note, my first pair of keens lasted about eight years and were amazing. they saw many destinations around the world. i retired them when the sole started separating in the back. my second pair only lasted a couple years and the sole of both completely delaminated and fell apart. even though the construction was seemingly on a downward trend, i ordered this replacement pair. i returned them immediately. if you still want keen sandals, consider trying their american made versions. i ended up with the rialto sandals. they don't fit quite as wide as my old newports, but they don't squeeze my feet or prevent splay either. the different feel took some getting used to, but they are much higher quality overall. they do have an insole that soaks up water and squishes as you walk, but it's not terrible and they still dry faster than a pair of shoes would.

I have yet to find others to fit my wide foot so I keep trying pair after pair.

TL DR 5 5 without integrity issue, 2.5 5 with integrity issues Pros Good traction even in the White Mountains Mt. Washington and comfort, great weight. Cons Quality and or Durability is lacking bad. Summary A well-balanced and favorited shoe that is tainted by its poor integrity.Recommendation Buy, but be warn that use, especially on rocking, high-elevation gain hikes, may lead to a short lifespan. Long Story So I m a weekend warrior hiker. Most of the time I stay in CT, with a White Mountain hike once a month, more or less. I ve been using ankle-supporting boot user since I started hiking, but I was forced to get sandals for the Narrows, so I got these. Didn t get to do the Narrows because of the water level, so I did Angel s Landing with them. I have converted to a sandal user ever since. However, my experience with the H2s hasn t been all positive. I m going to use other shoes I ve worn as comparisons to illustrate my pros and cons Merrell Moab Mids, KEEN Targhee III Mid, Saloman X Ultra Mid, and Brooks Cascadia 13s, with rankings in each section ranging from great, good, okay, lacking, to bad. - Traction Good. When I say good traction, I mean good traction once I learned how to hike with these. There was definitely a learning curve for me. Boot s weight and distribution of force make it so I don t have to really engage my feet when I hike, I just need to put my foot down. Hiking is just a walk with Moabs and Targhees. Not so with sandals. I have to think more, actually grip with my toes, take more consideration with my balance. It was kind of a turn off at first, because I was constantly slipping. This is a serious issue because the hikes I do always have steep sections. Wether it is Sleeping Giant s Blue Trail s 0.4 mi section up 500ft of slab or the 2,500 ft elevation gain bagging Mt. Tom and Mt. Field, I need shoes that will keep me grounded. All the initial slippage definitely made me miss heavy shoes with Vibram soles. But I don t turn tail unless I have to, so I kept pushing, and eventually I learned how to hike in these sandals. I would say traction plus skill on the H2s would be the same as my Targhees. Moabs, with their Vibram soles, have great traction, and are unrivaled in my experience. HOWEVER, the H2s have greater flexibility and a sleeker frame that allows me to stick my foot in holds and hop on uneven boulders that I wouldn t be able to do with boots. And, Unlike the lacking-traction Ultra Mids, I don t slide standing on smooth New England trap rock with the H2s. - Comfort Good. I used to be a big fan of Moabs because of the cushion. Those are the only hiking shoes I would rank great in comfort. The H2s are good for the complete opposite reason there is no cushion at all. Instead, there are just straps. Unlike an enclosed shoe, my ankle and heel can move freely, without worry of friction. Unlike plush, which wears and becomes a blister-friendly area, straps don t wear down, and can be better adjusted when my feet are swollen. I would have liked the ankle support to have better adjustability, but it was never a serious issue. The only reason why I wouldn t consider these shoes great in comfort is the toe box was too narrow for my toes, which are longer than normal toes. This wasn t an issue until I went downhill. Then my pinky toe would be bruised and bent to awkward angles. - Weight Great. Weight was an issue for a while since I was used to heavier shoes that needed less effort from me to push into for traction. Like I said before, there was learning curve for me. If not for my trekking poles I would have slid right off Wildcat Ridge trail. I no longer slip after a couple of mountains. I also used to use only boots because I was afraid of twisting my ankles and general injury. Come to find out, I hike better with less weight on my foot. I can confidently say twisting my ankle hasn t happened yet. Compared to nearly happening every three hikes with boots, this is definitely a plus. Take my other shoes as reference points. My Cascadias, which also rank great in weight, weighing a bit less than the H2s, are just plain uncomfortable to hike in. I always get bruises and blisters using them when doing 4 miles cuz' of my toes. My Ultra 3s, weighing a bit more than the H2s and ranking good in weight, have traction that is not suited for New England NY trap rock. - Quality and or Durability Lacking Bad. Man, these shoes were a let down when it came to durability. The toe box is solid, so no knock on those. I would say the shoe seemed put together until mile 80-ish. But come on, these shoes are UNUSABLE now after ONLY a 100 MILES of use. Fine, including 8 White Mountains Mt. Washington and Monroe up and down too! and steep parts of other hikes, 70 of those miles were tough on these shoes. But shoes shouldn t deteriorate like this. Last weekend, I went to the beach with my friends with the H2s on, and see what happened. The stitching came apart, something like cardboard came out, and the webbing, admittedly already breaking a bit due to descending the Jewell Trail, just kinda holed-up. The shoes are total fubar. This is sooo disappointing because the H2 became my favorite hiking shoe up until this point. I can t say whether it was a durability or quality issue, but this is ridiculous. My friend s plain Nikes, aside from being gym shoes, has been his go to for hikes CT and White Mountains for almost two years are in better shape than these. It may be a valid point to say these shoes weren t meant for the punishment I ve put them through, but I think there is a genuine problem when low-end Nikes hold better than the H2s under similar circumstances. The H2s balance traction, comfort, and weight to make hiking a more enjoyable experience, allowing me to hike longer. All the other shoes have their own balancing issues. My Targhees has good comfort and traction, but the weight is lacking. My Moabs have great traction and comfort, but bad weight I know they should be lighter than the Targhees, but they aren t for me on the trail . My Ultra 3s have good weight and comfort, but lacking traction which has lead to dangerous instances almost sliding off Mt. Marcy s summit . My Cascadias have good traction and great weight, but are not comfortable at all for my foot built long toes . The H2s are well balanced good traction, good comfort, and great weight. I just wish they were more durable. I don t want to keep buying H2s every two months. Maybe it was a singular instance of poor quality, I ll need to get in contact with KEEN to figure that out. But unfortunately, as is, I have to find another shoe for me.

In my Opinion these are the best sandals on the market. I only wish they would come in wide sizes for myself My kids have been wearing these since they started to walk

representative_reviews.text: I bought my first pair of these in 2016 and only this year did I decide to retire them. At the end, some of the leather near the ankles had worn through and the fabric looked like it was about to give. They were comfortable, they offered loads of traction, they were good looking, and after four years, I'd say they were durable as well. Fast forward to July 2020 I ordered a new pair. Same size, same color... still comfy, still look good, etc... the problem is the durability is just gone. It looks like the outsole and the insole are glued together pretty common afaik . The problem is that the outsole and the insole are separating at the points where the straps are glued in. After four months, my Keens already look like they're starting to fall apart. That just isn't acceptable as far as I'm concerned.
Came apart after using six times. Unbelievable. Will buy a cheap pair of Chinese knockoffs next time. Cannot equate quality with price these days.
The stitching came apart after just one season. Same place on both sandals. Emailed Keen support several times, never received a response.

i don't know what has happened to keen. i've been wearing their sandals since 2006 and this latest pair i ordered was complete junk. they fit way too tight and were very stiff. this is my fourth pair of keen newports in the same size, so i know exactly how they should fit. these were just wrong. i should also note, my first pair of keens lasted about eight years and were amazing. they saw many destinations around the world. i retired them when the sole started separating in the back. my second pair only lasted a couple years and the sole of both completely delaminated and fell apart. even though the construction was seemingly on a downward trend, i ordered this replacement pair. i returned them immediately. if you still want keen sandals, consider trying their american made versions. i ended up with the rialto sandals. they don't fit quite as wide as my old newports, but they don't squeeze my feet or prevent splay either. the different feel took some getting used to, but they are much higher quality overall. they do have an insole that soaks up water and squishes as you walk, but it's not terrible and they still dry faster than a pair of shoes would.

Broke after 5 days of use!!!!! So frustrated because the Keem brand is usually reliable. Can someone reply to my review? I feel I deserve a refund or replacement as these are not an inexpensive shoe it broke half way thru my camping trip. The heel strap completely broke and came out, it's not even repairable or stitchable!!! It was such a hassle for the second half of my trip. They're completely unusable now. Save your money!

I don't usually write reviews but thought that after my experience it was needed. I am now on my 4th pair of the same exact model, the KEEN Men's Newport H2 Sandal. With each pair, after only a few weeks of extremely light wear here and there I'm talking wearing to the grocery store for a few hours, not climbing or out in a river , the upper stitching of the sandals fell completely apart see pics . Warrantee replaced and it happened again, then I made the mistake of giving them the benefit of the doubt and purchasing again, only to have them fall apart for the 4th time in the very same place. Business school would teach a brand that if a product is continuously breaking down or coming apart in the same place it would be something worth working with customers to examine and find where the problem lies, that it would be a question of quality most likely in design, the manufacturing process, or the supply chain . However after the latest pair fell apart in the same place I was told they could no longer replace. Not a quality brand and does not stand by their product.

after 60-days of normal wear the stitching is coming undone on one of the straps... not real happy about this. there ought be a way to return them as this seams to be a problem with a few that have bought them.
These are the first time I've purchased new sandals amd they are falling apart. The stitching is tearing out and the straps are pulling out as well. It's such a shame

Upon receipt the sandals had dried glue on different areas of the sandals. Some of the straps had glue that looked like was coming undone. I do not know if the sandal was subject to heat prior to shipping that caused glue on this product to melt or if it was poor manufacturing. For a hundred dollars I expect higher quality. I'm returning the sandals and ordering a second pair. I'll update this review upon receipt of the new pair.

The fit, toe protection, and style were all pretty great, but after using 3-4 days a week for 3 weeks only about 10 days total , both sandals fell apart. I used them moderately for an internship at docks occasionally dunked in or splashed by seawater . Given that they're "water shoes" and by a very reputable company, I thought they'd last the summer and long afterwards. But the glue between insole and outsole lost its adhesive ability--the insole separated from the outsole on one sandal, while a heel strap slid out on the other sandal. I submitted photos from the day they broke to visualize and verify my description. I'm very disappointed with these KEEN sandals that cost about 100 for such low longevity. These sandals would have been awesome if only they'd lasted like one might expect. Now I'll buy cheap, mesh water shoes that may not offer as much protection, but they'll likely last longer and at 1 10 of the price. PLEASE read other low-satisfaction reviews before purchasing many other customers have had straps wear and adhesive fail after very little use.

I have had these for 18 months and they are coming apart. Despite little wear as can be seen on the pics. Very different than my previous Keen sandles. I reached out to Keen support was told to contact seller to arrange refund. Explained that window was past and was then ignored despite additional inquiries on my part. Sad part is my wife has a different model Keen sandle and it is coming apart too. Similar location on heel strap. After 15 years a customer, I will have to look to a different manufacturer.

VIDEOID 12473ae6fa2815ac8b880feafcb8ab39 I really used to like this brand Keen. Their quality has gone downhill I bought them in June. It is now September and they already have stitching coming out for paying over 100 I think they should last longer than this. I've never had a problem with this brand before but this makes me never want to buy this again a waste of money. It is past the date to return them I didn't know what to do
Only used 6 times and foot strap came apart. Guess thats what you get for a hundred bucks these days
Impossible to get them on!! Once on they fit ok. But there is no heal strap to unbuckle... making it virtually impossible to put on your feet. Poor design

VIDEOID 5137d8163f19a1522e6be85036f2424d We purchased 2 pair of these the end of May beginning of June 2020. Our 15 year old began wearing them immediately and had trouble with the material around the tongue tearing. Keen quickly replaced them. He began wearing the replacement sandals in April this year and they are doing the same thing. The tearing is on both sides of the tongue on both sandals. Our 13 year old has the other pair and rarely wears them, same issue. We purchased these because my 2 pair of Newport s have lasted 7 and 14 years. I have worn them rafting, hiking over miles of creek and hill trails as well as everyday wear during the summer. This is very frustrating as these are expensive and we expected them to hold up better than a pair of cheap flip flops. We are an active outdoor family during the summer and purchased these to allow the boys to run through all types of terrain. Now we will be looking at a different manufacturer for the 2 teens and 3 other boys.

Bought these as a gift for my husband who loves his Keen hiking boots so much that he bought a back-up pair of Keen boots. This is saying a lot because he's a forester, is in some kind of boot most of the time, and has tried them all. He has hard feet to size footwear for, as they're wide and also flat. Since this Keen brand seemed to work so well for him, I ordered 2 variations of these sandals as well as 2 sizes of each as a bday gift, so he'd be able to choose the best fit. The other Keen sandal I ordered was the original Keen sandal. I thought the older original and sized up would probably be the best fit for him best based on reviews I'd read, but it was these lighter lower profile sandals in his actual size not the sized up pair that fit him spot on!. A perfect match! And, with their lighter design, they looked way better on him than the heavier Keens. So happy these worked out -- they look great not too hulkish , and he loves them! A Plus is that these sandals ventilate well, and also cover up his bruised up toenails that he gets from year round field work on steep terrain in cleated hiking boots.
Product is sturdy and of high quality - exactly as advertised - I ll buy again, if there ever wear out!!

I wear these daily year round, on my 8th pair and love them. However, all of them fail at the same point in stitching. I add a couple of extra stitches there on my new ones and they last a lot longer. Kinda expected KEEN to address that design flaw by now. The bottom pair in the pic lasted through 20 National Parks and now I wear them remodeling the house.
Everyday shoe for me all year round... snow, rain or desert. I gorilla glue in a half sports foot-bed to eliminate my plantar factitious, otherwise stock.
My pair caused considerable abrasion on my toe top. Not as comfortable as I d hoped but construction seems solid.

Both my wife and I bought Keen water sandals. Both of ours disintegrated with less use than would be expected. Rubber falling apart or seams falling out We bought new ones because they were good while they be lasted, and we haven't found a suitable replacement.

I have a very hard time finding shoes and these are as good or better than the orthopedic sandals I had previously and are currently unavailable. We'll see how well they last but they appear very well made.

As I said my second pair, first pair lasted 5 years. I really like the enclosed toe sole. The toe protects your feet and the sole keeps you from slipping on wet surfaces. I am surprised by the support of the sandal, I wear them all day without any soreness or fatigue. I wear them year-round except for snow and ice. The sole is non-marking skiffed so they work well on wet boat surfaces. They look good with jeans or shorts. Buy 1 2 size up for good fit they will stretch out over time so don't worry. They are pricey but they go on sale holiday time, sometimes 1 2 price.

VIDEOID bb8142be007534ff64c2d0be5d38fe10 This is my second pair of the KEEN Newport Retro Sandals. I literally walked the tread off of the first pair - after wearing them pretty much daily for three years. I have had two other pairs of Newport Sandals. The black pair I also walked the tread off by wearing daily while living on the Big Island-Hawaii for three years. The Brown Newports - only two years old - I still have wear. They have been to the cobbler once to have the side straps reglued at the base a few months ago. They will be going back in a couple weeks for both soles to be reglued. They are flapping when I walk. Still - they are Most Excellent to the point I bought another pair in the Retro colors. Totally Happy Feet!
Well this here is my second pair of these bad boys. As you can see in the photo they held up well. Many miles and jokes in the first pair and I'm keen on doing the same with this pair...

Pretty sure this is my fourth pair from Keen. They have proven plenty durable by my standards. I have had two pair of sandals and two of the flip-flops. I used to work in the ski biz at a slope side shop that specialized in custom footbeds and boot work. These sandals are about as close as one can get to a true custom bed. They offer great support without being intrusive. I'm a fan for life, don't change a thing.
Husband has assorted foot ankle issues..good coverage for toes ,good support,can get wet.Just what he needed.

These are great! Comfortable, durable, gives your feet weird looking tan lines! The whole package! A little difficult to keep clean odorless if you have sweaty feet, and I recommend washing them in the sink to prolong the life of these. Also, you'll want to buy this 1 2 size bigger for optimal fit as they run slightly small. I've had mine for about 2 1 2 years and they have some good wear and tear on them, but are still holding up. I wear them while mowing, doing outside work in the summer, or pretty much everywhere. I did have to make a small repair to the part that has the Keen logo on it. I used some strong Upholstery thread and "shoe goo" to make the repair. That has held up well.
I am a big guy. 6'5'' 275. I have been looking for outdoor shoes that stay tight and supportive and I can transition from hiking to Dadding. Not sure I will ever buy any other shoes but these.

I ve had a pair of Keen sandals for a decade, so I needed another pair and ordered them. They last forever and they feel great. This new pair is a little heavier and chunkier than the last but they re breaking in well and feel good. It s a good product, my second pair, and I m happy with them.

representative_reviews.text: I had read about these in several places. They are awesome. Great hiking sandals. Far better than a pair of running shoes or sandals when a hiking boot is too hot or will hold water. I think they look ridiculously ugly, but they are very very good for hiking around or in water. My wife says they look fine. They really work well for what they do.

Bought my first pair of Keens a year ago and absolutely love them. Decided I wanted a second pair this year and ordered them. Apparently people thought these were the ugly ducklings because they were available and had the lowest price of all the rest. But as it turns out they are very attractive and fit perfectly.

Keen States What s not covered? Damage caused by normal wear and tear, improper care, misuse, accident, neglect, or the natural breakdown of materials over time... . Basically it cover nothing after arrival or 30 Day I guess so 30 Day its a Quality Policy, this is nothing for the produce cost, mine didn t last 2 months for 88 dlls .

I have been a huge fan of Keen shoes for the last 10 years up to now with this pair. After about 30 days of casual wear and a few short hikes the heel strap ripped exactly where other reviewers show see my pic in the pictures. After a few emails claim forms they credited me for a new pair to purchase from their website. However given this is an obvious defect built into the design I opted for the leather newport version which I had to pay 10 more for. Hopefully these will last. I should note that the shoe repair "cobbler" in my town mentioned he sees a lot of these Keen newports come in for repair. So why do they keep the same design contruction? Seems it would only take a simple cross stitch across the section that is prone to tearing.

I was told these were the sandals to buy and that they last a lifetime. Which is why inwas willing to spend the money. I have had them a smidge over a month and they are already falling apart. They coming apart at the seems. They are literally just simply falling apart. I am very disappointed and would not recommend anyone to buy these shoes. They are not worth the money at all. Completely disappointed. Nevwr again will I ever buy them.

Bought these keen sandals after talking with other patrons who love them. I liked them when i got them but after about one month, the elastic separated from the tongue at the seam on both sandals with normal wear. I spent 80 on these and really expected them to last for many years. Only lasted one month. Called Keen to find out about warranty. Very disappointing experience with customer service who showed zero empathy for a customer disappointed with Keen's product. Also, they were extremely difficult to talk to about the information I had with regard to my amazon transaction. Had to give one star but frankly poor product performance and poor customer service deserves zero stars.

I should have trusted the reviews and looked more at the defective pictures. I thought to myself, "Some of reviews are 4 years old and maybe they fixed the issues". Nope! I went out kayaking twice with these "water shoes" and they started falling apart. I was literally sitting all day without the pressure on the shoes. Somehow the stitching still fell apart on both shoes. I honestly thought I could trust the Keen brand with all of their styles. Quality is why they are so expensive right?

Size is NOT standard. These run extremely small! Husband wears a size 11 so, reading the advice to order up a size, I ordered a size 12 expecting the sandals to fit him. No way! A size 12 was still so narrow and so short he could hardly get the shoe on his foot. I measured the new size 12s to his old pair of size 11s same Keen brand, same model style and the new size 12 was visibly shorter and narrower than the old size 11. Shame on Keen. Why mess with a great product except to try and increase profits? No longer buying this brand as I have also heard the quality ha deteriorated badly. Small sizes and poor quality do not deserve top dollar prices.

This is my second paid. First pair lasted 4 years with daily use and lots of miles in all sort of terrain. These are incredibly well made and hope they never get discontinued. My well-being depends on them now.
You get what you pay for. Very comfortable walking long distances and they last for years. I wouldn t purchase any other brand, being so satisfied with my last pair.

Bought for my gf for Mother s Day. She absolutely loves them. She s never had Keens so I had to get her some. She has major foot problems so these were a blessing. She loves the support, the strudiness and the comfort. They look awesome with almost everything, jeans, dresses, shorts etc. super versatile.
Purchased keen in past. Always great quality and value. Amazing sandals for travel or daily use. These specific sandals did run a bit small, had to return and go up a size.

Bought for my husband because he loved the fit and comfort from his last pair, which finally wore out after a few years. The color and style are also perfect! He prefers sandals that cover his toes and can be worn hiking or to a restaurant - he is not a flip flop guy, so these fit the bill. As long as you don t expect them to last forever, these are awesome!

Good price on Keen sandals. Ordered 1 2 size up as other reviewers suggested .Arrived in perfect shape. The person these are for had another pair of Keens for years, and finally wore them out. This grey color is flexible to go with many colors.

seemed a little pricey but had good reviews. took the flier and ordered my regular size. seemed a little tight at first but loosened up and fit great. these shoes are very comfortable and seem very durable. glad i made the purchase.

Great design and my son loves! I ordered up per the Keen website and glad I did, he would normally be a 9.50 but ordered the 10 and its a good fit for my 12 year old. These will serve him well at camp this summer!

I thought these were overpriced for sandals, but a friend talked me into them. I'm glad he did-- they're super comfortable, very light, and have a great tread. The insole is a high-density foam the provides great support, and the fit adjusts really easily. I really like the colors, and it's great that they carried the color scheme onto the outer sole, too.

Bought my first pair of Keens a year ago and absolutely love them. Decided I wanted a second pair this year and ordered them. Apparently people thought these were the ugly ducklings because they were available and had the lowest price of all the rest. But as it turns out they are very attractive and fit perfectly.
